title: Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: African Union Commission (endorsed by the AU Executive Council)
summary_plain: A continental framework that guides AU member states on harnessing AI for development while managing risks. It is organised around five focus areas: capturing AI benefits, building capabilities, minimising risks, stimulating investment, and fostering cooperation. It is non-binding and intended to inform national strategies and regional harmonisation.

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle de l'Algérie
issuing_body: Government of Algeria
summary_plain: The strategy sets priorities on AI talent and research, start-ups, public-sector and industrial adoption, data and compute, and governance through the National AI Council.

title: Decisión Administrativa 899/2024 – Mesa Interministerial sobre Inteligencia Artificial (Administrative Decision 899/2024 – Interministerial Board on Artificial Intelligence)
issuing_body: Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
summary_plain: This administrative decision restructures the Interministerial Board on AI originally created in 2023, placing it under the presidency of the Secretariat of Innovation, Science and Technology and expanding its membership to ministries including Defence, Economy, Foreign Affairs, Health, Security, Human Capital, Justice and State Deregulation. The board is tasked with coordinating the government's approach to AI adoption across economic and social sectors and with developing national strategies. Argentina has not yet adopted a standalone national AI strategy or a binding AI law.
source_publisher: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina

title: Disposición 2/2023 – Recomendaciones para una Inteligencia Artificial Fiable (Disposition 2/2023 – Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence)
issuing_body: Subsecretaría de Tecnologías de la Información, Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
summary_plain: Disposición 2/2023 approves a set of recommendations for trustworthy AI addressed to projects designed, developed or adopted by the national public sector, together with a diagram of the stages of an AI project. Aligned with the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, it emphasises human-centred design, transparency, human oversight, non-discrimination, data protection and accountability across the project lifecycle. It is guidance rather than a binding regulatory regime.

title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics – Generative AI
short_title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics – Generative AI (2025)
issuing_body: ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting
summary_plain: Endorsed in January 2025, the expanded guide addresses risks specific to generative AI (hallucination, deepfakes and misinformation, intellectual property, privacy, security, bias, embedded values) and proposes governance dimensions covering accountability, data, development and deployment, incident reporting, testing and assurance, security, content provenance, safety research and public-interest use, with policy recommendations for member states.

title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
short_title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics (2024)
issuing_body: ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting
summary_plain: Endorsed at the 4th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting in February 2024, the guide sets seven guiding principles (transparency and explainability, fairness and equity, security and safety, human-centricity, privacy and data governance, accountability and integrity, robustness and reliability) and a four-part governance framework (internal governance structures, human involvement in decision-making, operations management, stakeholder interaction), with national and regional recommendations including an ASEAN working group on AI governance.

title: Proposals paper: introducing mandatory guardrails for AI in high-risk settings (Australia)
issuing_body: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
summary_plain: The proposals paper sought views on ten mandatory guardrails for developers and deployers of AI in high-risk settings, a principles-based definition of high-risk AI (with general-purpose AI treated as high-risk), and three regulatory options: adapting existing laws, framework legislation, or a new cross-economy AI Act. The guardrails mirror the Voluntary AI Safety Standard, covering accountability, risk management, data governance, testing, human control, transparency, contestability, supply-chain transparency, records, and conformity assessment.
who_it_applies_to: Prospectively, developers and deployers of high-risk AI in Australia; currently no one.
source_publisher: Australian Government, Department of Industry, Science and Resources

title: National AI Plan
issuing_body: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
summary_plain: The National AI Plan is the Australian Government's whole-of-government AI strategy with three goals: capture the opportunity through infrastructure, domestic capability and investment; spread the benefits through adoption, skills and better public services; and keep Australians safe through legal and regulatory frameworks and responsible-practice guidance. It consolidates existing AI funding commitments and signals a sector-by-sector regulatory approach supported by an AI Safety Institute, rather than a standalone AI act.
source_publisher: Department of Industry, Science and Resources

title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard (Australia)
issuing_body: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
summary_plain: The Voluntary AI Safety Standard gives Australian organisations ten guardrails for developing and deploying AI safely and responsibly: accountability and governance, risk management, data governance and protection, testing and monitoring, human control and intervention, user transparency, contestability, supply-chain transparency, record keeping, and stakeholder engagement. The guardrails were designed to align with the mandatory guardrails proposed for high-risk settings so that early adopters would be prepared if those became law.
who_it_applies_to: Any Australian organisation deploying or developing AI (voluntary), with practical focus on deployers.
source_publisher: Australian Government, Department of Industry, Science and Resources

title: Strategie der Bundesregierung für Künstliche Intelligenz – Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030 (AIM AT 2030)
issuing_body: Federal Government of Austria
summary_plain: Adopted in August 2021, AIM AT 2030 sets three objectives: broad use of AI oriented to the common good and fundamental rights, Austria as a research and innovation location, and competitiveness of the Austrian technology and business location. It lists fields of action including trustworthy AI, public administration, skills, data and infrastructure, with an implementation and monitoring structure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Republic of Azerbaijan for 2025–2028 (presidential decree, March 2025)
issuing_body: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
summary_plain: Approved by presidential decree in March 2025, the strategy sets goals for AI in public administration, the economy and education, data and computing infrastructure, talent, ethical and safe AI, and a coordinating institutional structure, with an action plan to 2028.

title: General Policy for the Use of Artificial Intelligence
short_title: General Policy for the Use of Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Information & eGovernment Authority (iGA)
summary_plain: A binding policy for Bahraini government entities structured around four pillars: compliance with AI-related laws and policies (including the Personal Data Protection Law and the GCC AI ethics guide), use and adoption of AI technologies, awareness and education, and local and international cooperation. It defines roles and responsibilities for entities and assigns oversight to iGA. Alongside the policy, Bahrain adopted the GCC Guiding Manual on the Ethics of AI Use.
source_publisher: Information & eGovernment Authority, Kingdom of Bahrain

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026-2030 (Draft V2.0)
issuing_body: ICT Division, Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology
summary_plain: A revised draft national AI policy published by the ICT Division for public review. It proposes a risk-based approach to AI regulation with prohibitions on certain uses, impact assessments for high-risk systems, and institutional arrangements for coordination and capacity building. Public consultation on the draft closed in February 2026 and the committee is reviewing submissions before finalisation.

title: Plan national de convergence pour le développement de l'intelligence artificielle
issuing_body: Federal Government of Belgium with the Regions and Communities
summary_plain: Adopted in 2022, the convergence plan coordinates the federal and regional AI initiatives around nine objectives, including trustworthy AI, skills, data, research, public-sector adoption and international positioning, with AI4Belgium as the delivery coalition.

title: Stratégie nationale d'intelligence artificielle et des mégadonnées 2023–2027
short_title: National AI and Big Data Strategy 2023–2027
issuing_body: Government of Benin (Ministry of Digital Affairs and Digitalisation)
summary_plain: Adopted by the Council of Ministers in January 2023, the strategy sets objectives for AI and big-data skills, research, data infrastructure and governance, ethical AI and priority use cases in health, education, agriculture, tourism and living environment, with a 2027 horizon.
source_publisher: Ministère du Numérique et de la Digitalisation

title: Bhutan National AI Strategy 2025 (NAIS 2025)
issuing_body: GovTech Agency, Royal Government of Bhutan
summary_plain: A national strategy framed around the vision of AI rooted in Gross National Happiness. It identifies eight focus areas (agriculture and livestock, tourism, green energy, education, health, public service delivery, natural resources and biodiversity, and culture and language) and seven enablers such as infrastructure, governance and regulation, cybersecurity, skills, research, collaboration and funding. It aims to raise Bhutan's AI maturity by the end of the 13th Five Year Plan and includes monitoring, evaluation and risk-mitigation provisions.
source_publisher: GovTech Agency, Royal Government of Bhutan

title: Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial 2024-2028 – PBIA (Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan 2024-2028)
issuing_body: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (MCTI) with the Conselho Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia (CCT)
summary_plain: The PBIA is a four-year national plan that commits around R$23 billion to AI infrastructure, skills, public-sector applications, business innovation and governance. Headline measures include acquiring a top-tier supercomputer powered by renewable energy, developing Portuguese-language models, and short-term actions in health, education, agriculture and public services. The proposal was presented at the 5th National Conference on Science, Technology and Innovation and formally approved by the CCT through Resolução CCT nº 4/2024, with a final version later published under MCTI coordination.
source_publisher: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (gov.br)

title: Projeto de Lei nº 2338/2023 – Dispõe sobre o uso da Inteligência Artificial (Bill No. 2338/2023 – On the use of Artificial Intelligence)
issuing_body: Senado Federal (author: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco); now before the Câmara dos Deputados
summary_plain: PL 2338/2023 is Brazil's flagship AI bill, introduced in the Senate in May 2023 and approved by the Senate plenary on 10 December 2024 after extensive amendment. It classifies AI systems by risk, bans certain uses, sets obligations for developers and deployers of high-risk systems, and provides for rights of affected persons and a national governance system. The Senate transmitted the text to the Chamber of Deputies on 17 March 2025, where a special committee is examining it.

title: Концепция за развитието на изкуствения интелект в България до 2030 г.
short_title: Concept for the development of AI until 2030
issuing_body: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria
summary_plain: Adopted in December 2020, the concept sets a framework for AI in Bulgaria to 2030 in line with the EU coordinated plan: research and infrastructure, skills, data, adoption in business and public administration, and trustworthy, ethical AI.

title: Strengthening Cyber Security and Building Trust in the Public Sector Act, 2024 (Bill 194), Schedule 1: Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024
short_title: Ontario Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024 (Bill 194)
issuing_body: Legislative Assembly of Ontario
summary_plain: The Act allows the Ontario government to make regulations governing the use of AI systems by public-sector entities (ministries, agencies, hospitals, school boards, municipalities as prescribed): requirements to disclose AI use, to develop and implement accountability frameworks, to take steps to manage risks, to have human oversight, and prohibitions on prescribed uses. It also addresses cyber security and children's digital information.

title: Working for Workers Four Act, 2024 (Bill 149): disclosure of artificial intelligence use in publicly advertised job postings
short_title: Ontario Working for Workers Four Act (AI disclosure in job postings)
issuing_body: Legislative Assembly of Ontario
summary_plain: Amends the Employment Standards Act, 2000 to require employers with 25 or more employees to disclose in every publicly advertised job posting whether artificial intelligence is used to screen, assess or select applicants, alongside new rules on salary ranges and Canadian-experience requirements. The AI disclosure requirement is in force from 1 January 2026.

title: Quebec Law 25 (S.Q. 2021, c. 25): provisions on decisions based exclusively on automated processing and biometric systems
issuing_body: National Assembly of Quebec
summary_plain: Section 12.1 of the private-sector privacy act (as amended by Law 25, in force 22 September 2023) requires any enterprise that uses personal information to render a decision based exclusively on automated processing to inform the person no later than when the decision is made, and, on request, to tell them what personal information was used, the reasons and principal factors and parameters, and their right to have the information corrected, and to give them an opportunity to submit observations to a person who can review the decision. Biometric identification databases must be declared to the Commission d'accès à l'information 60 days before use, and privacy impact assessments are mandatory for projects involving personal information. Penalties reach CAD 25 million or 4% of worldwide turnover.

title: Cambodia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Government of Cambodia (MPTC and MISTI)
summary_plain: A national AI strategy and ethics framework under preparation with UNESCO support, expected to cover governance, talent, public-sector use and the digital economy.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (Part 3 of Bill C-27, Digital Charter Implementation Act, 2022)
issuing_body: Parliament of Canada (sponsored by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry)
summary_plain: The Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA) was proposed as Part 3 of Bill C-27 and would have required organisations designing, developing or deploying high-impact AI systems to assess and mitigate risks of harm and bias, keep records and publish information, with enforcement by an AI and Data Commissioner and penalties for serious offences. The bill passed second reading in the House of Commons in April 2023 and was studied in committee through 2024 but never advanced to report stage. It lapsed when the 44th Parliament ended in early 2025 without the bill being passed.

title: Pan-Canadian Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
summary_plain: The Pan-Canadian AI Strategy is Canada's national AI strategy, first funded in Budget 2017 with $125 million and delivered largely through CIFAR and three national AI institutes. A second phase from 2021 added funding for commercialisation, standards and computing capacity, with further support in the 2024 Fall Economic Statement. It focuses on attracting and retaining researchers, translating research into industry adoption and promoting responsible AI.
source_publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
short_title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
issuing_body: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
summary_plain: This voluntary code asks Canadian developers and managers of advanced generative AI systems to commit to measures under six principles: accountability, safety, fairness and equity, transparency, human oversight and monitoring, and validity and robustness. Obligations are scaled according to whether a system is made available for general public use. It was introduced as a bridge while the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act was before Parliament, and lists around fifty signatory organisations.
source_publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

title: Política Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial – Actualización 2024 y Plan de Acción (National Artificial Intelligence Policy – 2024 Update and Action Plan)
issuing_body: Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología, Conocimiento e Innovación (MinCiencia)
summary_plain: Chile updated its 2021 National AI Policy in 2024, keeping the ten-year horizon to 2031 but reorienting it around ethics, governance and inclusion after a participatory process across the country's regions. The accompanying action plan lists 177 initiatives coordinated by 14 ministries under axes covering enabling factors, development and adoption, and governance and ethics, with periodic progress reporting. The update was presented on 2 May 2024 together with the announcement of a government bill to regulate AI systems.
source_publisher: Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología, Conocimiento e Innovación

title: Proyecto de ley que regula los sistemas de inteligencia artificial, Boletín 16821-19 (Bill regulating artificial intelligence systems, Bulletin 16821-19)
short_title: Proyecto de ley que regula los sistemas de inteligencia artificial, Boletín 16821-19
issuing_body: Presidencia de la República (Mensaje) / Congreso Nacional (Cámara de Diputadas y Diputados; Senado)
summary_plain: Introduced by presidential message in May 2024 and merged with an earlier parliamentary motion (Boletín 15869-19), the bill classifies AI system uses into unacceptable, high, limited and no-evident-risk categories, prohibits certain practices, and sets obligations, incident reporting and sanctions. It creates a Technical Advisory Council on AI to advise MinCiencia and proposes periodic review of the law. The Chamber of Deputies approved the text in October 2025 and it is now in second constitutional stage before the Senate's Future Challenges, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee.
source_publisher: Senado de la República de Chile

title: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
short_title: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China with NDRC, Ministry of Education, MOST, MIIT, Ministry of Public Security and NRTA
summary_plain: These measures govern generative AI services offered to the public in China, whether producing text, images, audio or video. Providers must use lawfully sourced training data, take steps against discrimination, protect personal information, label generated content, handle user complaints and ensure outputs comply with content rules. Services with public-opinion or social-mobilisation capacity must complete security assessments and algorithm filing. The measures took effect on 15 August 2023.

title: Measures for Labeling Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Synthetic Content
short_title: Measures for Labeling Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Synthetic Content
issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China with MIIT, Ministry of Public Security and NRTA
summary_plain: These measures require providers of AI generation and synthesis services to attach explicit labels (visible text, audio or graphic notices) and implicit labels (embedded metadata) to generated text, images, audio, video and virtual scenes. Platforms distributing content must check for and preserve labels, users must declare AI-generated material, and removing or forging labels is prohibited. Compliance is checked during algorithm filing and security assessments. The measures took effect on 1 September 2025.

title: Opinions of the State Council on Deepening the Implementation of the 'AI Plus' Action
short_title: Opinions of the State Council on Deepening the Implementation of the 'AI Plus' Action
issuing_body: State Council of the People's Republic of China
summary_plain: This State Council policy document (Guofa [2025] No. 11) sets national targets for AI adoption: broad integration in six priority areas and over 70 percent penetration of intelligent terminals and agents by 2027, over 90 percent by 2030, and a fully intelligent economy and society by 2035. It directs actions in science and technology, industry, consumption, public welfare, governance and international cooperation, backed by measures on models, data, computing infrastructure, talent, law and safety. It succeeds the 2017 New Generation AI Development Plan as the current headline national AI strategy.
source_publisher: Central People's Government of the PRC (gov.cn)

title: Documento CONPES 4144 – Política Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (CONPES Document 4144 – National Artificial Intelligence Policy)
issuing_body: Consejo Nacional de Política Económica y Social (CONPES) / Departamento Nacional de Planeación (DNP)
summary_plain: CONPES 4144, approved on 14 February 2025, is Colombia's national AI policy and roadmap through 2030. It sets objectives on governance and ethics, data and infrastructure, research and talent, and adoption across the public and private sectors, backed by an action plan of more than 100 actions with assigned entities and an indicative budget. The DNP, MinTIC, Minciencias and several line ministries share responsibility for its execution and monitoring.
source_publisher: Ministerio de Tecnologías de la Información y las Comunicaciones (normograma) – DNP document

title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial de Costa Rica 2024–2027
issuing_body: Government of Costa Rica (MICITT)
summary_plain: Launched in October 2024, the strategy sets pillars on governance and ethics, talent and skills, research and innovation, infrastructure and data, and adoption in the public sector and productive sectors, with an action plan to 2027 informed by UNESCO's Readiness Assessment Methodology.

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle de la Côte d'Ivoire
issuing_body: Government of Côte d'Ivoire
summary_plain: The strategy sets priorities on AI talent and research, adoption in public services, agriculture, health and education, data governance and infrastructure, and ethical use.

title: Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225)
issuing_body: Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe
summary_plain: The first international treaty on AI. Parties must adopt or maintain measures so that activities within the lifecycle of AI systems are consistent with human rights, democracy and the rule of law, covering public authorities and actors on their behalf and, by choice of approach, private actors. It sets principles (human dignity and autonomy, transparency and oversight, accountability, equality and non-discrimination, privacy, reliability, safe innovation), requires remedies, procedural safeguards and risk and impact assessment, allows moratoria or bans for incompatible uses, and creates a Conference of the Parties for follow-up. National-security activities and defence are excluded.
who_it_applies_to: States and the EU that ratify; public authorities and private actors through implementing measures.

title: Methodology for the Risk and Impact Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Systems from the Point of View of Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (HUDERIA)
short_title: HUDERIA risk and impact assessment methodology
issuing_body: Council of Europe Committee on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
summary_plain: Adopted by the CAI in November 2024, HUDERIA is a structured methodology for assessing risks and impacts of AI systems on human rights, democracy and the rule of law across the lifecycle: context-based risk analysis, stakeholder engagement, risk and impact assessment, and mitigation planning with iterative review. It supports implementation of the Framework Convention and can be used by public and private organisations.

title: Nacionalni plan razvoja umjetne inteligencije
short_title: National Plan for the Development of AI
issuing_body: Government of Croatia (Central State Office for the Development of the Digital Society)
summary_plain: The national AI plan sets priorities for research, skills, public-sector and business adoption, data and infrastructure and trustworthy AI in line with the EU coordinated plan and the AI Act.

title: Estrategia para el desarrollo y uso de la inteligencia artificial en Cuba
issuing_body: Government of Cuba (Ministry of Communications)
summary_plain: The strategy sets principles for the ethical development and use of AI in Cuba, priorities for public administration, health and education, and a governance structure led by the Ministry of Communications.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Republic of Cyprus
issuing_body: Council of Ministers of Cyprus
summary_plain: Approved in January 2020 and updated by an action plan in 2024, the strategy covers research, skills, data and infrastructure, public-sector and business adoption, and ethical, trustworthy AI aligned with the EU framework.
source_publisher: Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy

title: Národní strategie umělé inteligence České republiky 2030
issuing_body: Government of the Czech Republic (Ministry of Industry and Trade)
summary_plain: Approved by the government in July 2024, the strategy to 2030 replaces the 2019 strategy and sets priorities on research and innovation, skills, infrastructure and data, industry and public-sector adoption, trustworthy AI and AI Act implementation, with measurable goals and a governance structure.

title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Government of Denmark (Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs)
summary_plain: Published in March 2019, the strategy sets a responsible foundation for AI (ethical principles, data ethics council, legal clarity), more and better data, strong competences and new knowledge, and increased investment, with priority sectors of health, energy and utilities, agriculture and transport, and a set of public-sector pilot projects.

title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial de la República Dominicana (ENIA)
issuing_body: Government of the Dominican Republic (OGTIC)
summary_plain: Adopted in 2023, ENIA sets objectives on ethical and responsible AI, talent development, AI in public services and priority sectors (health, education, tourism, security), data infrastructure and research, with a governance committee and action plan.

title: Proyecto de Ley Orgánica de Regulación y Promoción de la Inteligencia Artificial
issuing_body: National Assembly of Ecuador
summary_plain: The draft organic law proposes principles for AI (human-centric, transparency, non-discrimination, safety), a risk-based classification with prohibited and high-risk uses, obligations for developers and deployers, a national AI authority and sanctions, drawing on the EU AI Act and UNESCO recommendation.

title: Egypt National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
summary_plain: Egypt's first national AI strategy framed AI as a tool for the country's sustainable development goals and for positioning Egypt as an active contributor to AI in Africa and the Arab region. It covered AI for government, development, capacity building and international activities. It has been superseded by the 2025-2030 second edition.
source_publisher: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, Egypt

title: National AI Strategy - Second Edition 2025-2030
issuing_body: National Council for Artificial Intelligence (NCAI), Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
summary_plain: The second edition updates Egypt's 2021 strategy for 2025-2030 around six pillars: governance, data, infrastructure, technology, talent and ecosystem. It sets targets for AI specialists, startups and ICT's contribution to GDP, and includes plans for national foundational models and expanded regional and international cooperation.
source_publisher: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, Egypt

title: Ley para el Fomento de la Inteligencia Artificial y Tecnologías Emergentes (Decreto Legislativo, febrero de 2025)
short_title: Law for the Promotion of AI and Emerging Technologies
issuing_body: Asamblea Legislativa de El Salvador
summary_plain: Approved by the Legislative Assembly in February 2025, the law promotes AI development and investment, creates the National Agency for Artificial Intelligence (ANIA) as regulator, defines rights and principles (human oversight, transparency, non-discrimination, data protection), sets registration and sandbox mechanisms and limits liability of developers who act in good faith under the law, alongside data-processing rules for AI training.

title: Eesti tehisintellekti tegevuskava 2024–2026 (Estonia's national AI action plan)
issuing_body: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
summary_plain: The third Estonian AI action plan continues the "kratt" programme: adoption of AI in public services and the Bürokratt virtual-assistant ecosystem, support for private-sector use, skills and research, data availability, and preparation for the EU AI Act, including public-sector guidelines on generative AI.
source_publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy of Ethiopia
issuing_body: Council of Ministers of Ethiopia (Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute)
summary_plain: Approved by the Council of Ministers in 2024, the policy sets objectives for AI research and talent, adoption in agriculture, health, education, security and public services, data governance and infrastructure, and ethical, responsible use, with the Ethiopian AI Institute as implementing body.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — Artificial Intelligence Act
issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
summary_plain: The EU AI Act is a binding regulation that sets rules for developing, placing on the market and using AI systems in the European Union. It bans a small set of practices considered unacceptable, imposes detailed requirements on "high-risk" AI systems used in areas such as employment, education, credit, essential services, law enforcement and safety-critical products, requires transparency for chatbots and synthetic content, and creates separate duties for providers of general-purpose AI models. Obligations apply in phases between 2025 and 2028.
who_it_applies_to: Providers (developers), deployers (organisations using AI under their authority), importers, distributors, authorised representatives of non-EU providers, product manufacturers integrating AI, and providers of general-purpose AI models. Public authorities are covered as deployers and have extra duties for fundamental-rights impact assessments.
source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

title: Apply AI Strategy
issuing_body: European Commission (DG CONNECT)
summary_plain: The Apply AI Strategy is a Commission communication that sets out how the EU intends to speed up use of AI across ten strategic sectors (such as healthcare, manufacturing, energy, mobility and defence) and in public administration. It combines sectoral flagship initiatives with cross-cutting support such as AI Factories, testing facilities and skills measures, and creates an Apply AI Alliance to coordinate industry, academia and public bodies. It sits within the broader AI Continent Action Plan and was presented together with a companion AI in Science strategy.
source_publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future

title: Finland's Age of Artificial Intelligence: Turning Finland into a leading country in the application of AI (objective and recommendations for measures)
issuing_body: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment of Finland
summary_plain: The 2017 report of the steering group appointed by the Minister of Economic Affairs proposed eight key actions to make Finland a leader in applying AI: enhancing business competitiveness, using data in all sectors, faster adoption, top-level expertise and talent, bold decisions and investments, the best public services, new cooperation models and a human-centred approach. It launched the national AI programme continued in the 2019 final report and the AI 4.0 programme.
source_publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment

title: CNIL recommendations on the development of AI systems and the GDPR (AI how-to sheets)
issuing_body: Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL)
summary_plain: A series of practical guidance sheets, first published in 2024 and extended since, explaining how organisations can develop and train AI systems in compliance with the GDPR: defining a purpose, choosing a legal basis (including legitimate interest for web-scraped training data), data minimisation, retention, data-protection impact assessments, informing people and honouring their rights, and security of training datasets and models.

title: Stratégie nationale pour l'intelligence artificielle (National AI Strategy, phases 1–3, 2018–2025)
issuing_body: Government of France (Ministry of the Economy, SGPI)
summary_plain: Launched in March 2018 following the Villani report, the national AI strategy funds research institutes (3IA then AI clusters), talent, compute and business adoption. The second phase (2021) focused on training and diffusion into the economy; the third phase (2024–2025) emphasises sovereign generative-AI models, compute and public-sector use, and framed France's hosting of the AI Action Summit in February 2025.
source_publisher: Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique

title: Entwurf eines Gesetzes zur Durchführung der KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsförderungsgesetz, KI-MIG)
issuing_body: Federal Ministry for Digital and State Modernisation
summary_plain: The draft implementation act designates the Bundesnetzagentur as the central market-surveillance authority and single point of contact under the EU AI Act, keeps sector regulators (financial supervision, data protection for law-enforcement uses) competent in their fields, sets the national penalty framework within the Regulation's ranges and creates a national AI regulatory sandbox and an AI service desk for companies.

title: Strategie Künstliche Intelligenz der Bundesregierung (AI Strategy of the Federal Government, 2018, updated 2020)
short_title: AI Strategy of the Federal Government
issuing_body: Federal Government of Germany (BMBF, BMWK, BMAS)
summary_plain: The federal AI strategy, adopted in November 2018 and updated in December 2020, sets out how Germany intends to make AI research, transfer and use competitive while anchoring AI in fundamental rights and the common good. The 2020 update raised planned federal funding to around EUR 5 billion to 2025 and added priorities on pandemic response, sustainability, health, mobility and AI in the public sector. It commits to a European approach to AI regulation and to trustworthy-AI standards.

title: Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025-2035)
issuing_body: Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations
summary_plain: A ten-year national roadmap launched by President Mahama that treats data as a national asset and sets out pillars covering education and skills, infrastructure and compute, data governance, ecosystem development, sector adoption, applied research and public-sector AI. It proposes a National AI Fund and performance indicators for ministries, and emphasises localisation of AI for Ghanaian languages.
source_publisher: Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Ghana

title: A Blueprint for Greece's AI Transformation – report of the AI Advisory Committee
issuing_body: AI Advisory Committee to the Prime Minister of Greece
summary_plain: Delivered in November 2024, the Advisory Committee's report proposes a national AI strategy: public-sector AI deployment, AI in health, education and agriculture, sovereign Greek language models, compute, skills, regulatory sandboxes and governance aligned with the EU AI Act.

title: Νόμος 4961/2022: Αναδυόμενες τεχνολογίες πληροφορικής και επικοινωνιών, ενίσχυση της ψηφιακής διακυβέρνησης και άλλες διατάξεις
issuing_body: Hellenic Parliament
summary_plain: Law 4961/2022, published in July 2022, contains a chapter on artificial intelligence: public-sector bodies must carry out an algorithmic impact assessment and publish information before deploying AI systems that affect people, keep a register of AI systems, and ensure the Hellenic Data Protection Authority's oversight; medium and large private companies must inform workers about AI systems used in employment decisions and maintain an ethical-use policy. It also regulates IoT, 3D printing, blockchain and unmanned aircraft.

title: Rome Call for AI Ethics (Pontifical Academy for Life, 28 February 2020)
issuing_body: Pontifical Academy for Life (RenAIssance Foundation)
summary_plain: A declaration of six principles for the ethical development of AI (transparency, inclusion, responsibility, impartiality, reliability, security and privacy), first signed in February 2020 by the Pontifical Academy for Life, Microsoft, IBM, FAO and the Italian government, and since joined by other religious leaders, universities and companies. It calls for "algor-ethics" and human-centred design and is used as a reference in faith-based and corporate AI ethics commitments.
source_publisher: RenAIssance Foundation / Pontifical Academy for Life

title: Hong Kong Generative Artificial Intelligence Technical and Application Guideline
short_title: Generative AI Technical and Application Guideline (2025)
issuing_body: Digital Policy Office, with the Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Centre
summary_plain: Published in April 2025, the guideline covers the technical characteristics and risks of generative AI, governance principles (safety, transparency, accountability, data protection, fairness) and practical application guidance for developers, service providers and users across the AI lifecycle, and is intended as a reference for industry and government.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Model Personal Data Protection Framework
short_title: PCPD Model Personal Data Protection Framework for AI (2024)
issuing_body: Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data, Hong Kong
summary_plain: Published 11 June 2024, the framework gives organisations that procure, implement and use AI systems involving personal data recommendations in four areas: AI strategy and governance (an AI governance committee, procurement due diligence), risk assessment and human oversight (a risk-based approach with levels of human involvement), customisation and implementation of AI models (data preparation, testing, security), and communication and engagement with stakeholders (transparency, explainability, opt-out, feedback). It builds on the 2021 Guidance on the Ethical Development and Use of AI.

title: Magyarország Mesterséges Intelligencia Stratégiája 2020–2030
issuing_body: Government of Hungary (Ministry for Innovation and Technology)
summary_plain: Adopted in September 2020, the strategy sets goals to 2030 on data economy, AI research and education, public-sector and industrial adoption, and transformative programmes such as an AI-driven public administration and language technology, coordinated with the AI Coalition of companies, universities and public bodies.

title: Aðgerðaáætlun um gervigreind 2024–2026 (Action plan on artificial intelligence)
issuing_body: Government of Iceland
summary_plain: The 2024–2026 action plan implements Iceland's AI policy with measures on AI in public services, the Icelandic language in AI systems, skills and research, ethics and security, and preparation for the EU AI Act.

title: India AI Governance Guidelines (MeitY, 2025)
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
summary_plain: The India AI Governance Guidelines set out a principle-based, pro-innovation approach to governing AI in India. They articulate guiding principles (such as trust, people-first design, fairness, accountability, safety and transparency), propose an institutional framework including an AI governance group and an AI Safety Institute role, favour applying existing laws over a new AI statute, and recommend voluntary commitments, techno-legal measures, risk-based oversight and incident reporting for AI systems.
who_it_applies_to: Indian government agencies, AI developers, deployers and platforms operating in India (voluntary).
source_publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
source_reference: Direct document link to be added by reviewer

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025
issuing_body: Parliament of India; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Rules)
summary_plain: The DPDP Act is India's cross-sector personal-data law. It applies to digital personal data processed in India and to processing outside India connected with offering goods or services to people in India. It requires a lawful basis (consent or specified legitimate uses), notice, purpose limitation, data accuracy, security safeguards, breach notification to the Data Protection Board and affected individuals, and grants rights of access, correction, erasure and grievance redress. Significant Data Fiduciaries face extra duties such as impact assessments and audits. The Act does not mention AI specifically, but it governs the personal data used to train and operate AI systems.
who_it_applies_to: Any organisation processing digital personal data of individuals in India, including AI developers and deployers using such data.
source_publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India

title: IndiaAI Mission
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Union Cabinet approval)
summary_plain: A five-year national programme approved by the Union Cabinet with an outlay of about INR 10,372 crore. It funds shared public AI compute (10,000+ GPUs), an innovation centre for indigenous foundation models, a datasets platform, application development for public problems, skilling programmes, startup financing and work on safe and trusted AI. Implementation is handled by the IndiaAI division of Digital India Corporation.
source_publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India (Cabinet decision)

title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (#AIforAll)
issuing_body: NITI Aayog
summary_plain: A discussion paper that set out India's first national approach to artificial intelligence. It prioritises five sectors (healthcare, agriculture, education, smart cities and infrastructure, and smart mobility) and proposes research institutions, data ecosystems and skilling measures to support adoption. It also flags privacy, fairness and explainability as issues needing attention and recommends institutional structures for responsible AI.

title: Rancangan Peraturan Presiden tentang Peta Jalan Kecerdasan Artifisial Nasional 2026-2029 (Draft Presidential Regulation on the National AI Roadmap)
short_title: Rancangan Peraturan Presiden tentang Peta Jalan Kecerdasan Artifisial Nasional 2026-2029
issuing_body: Ministry of Communication and Digital (Komdigi)
summary_plain: A draft presidential regulation, prepared under Presidential Decree No. 38 of 2025, that would establish a binding national AI roadmap for 2026-2029 alongside a companion draft regulation on AI ethics. Inter-ministerial discussion agreed four policy directions: stakeholder engagement, innovation, technology and research capability, and risk mitigation. Cross-ministry deliberations concluded in May 2026 and both drafts were submitted to the President for enactment.

title: Strategi Nasional Kecerdasan Artifisial Indonesia 2020-2045 (National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence)
issuing_body: Agency for the Assessment and Application of Technology (BPPT), now part of BRIN
summary_plain: Indonesia's long-range national AI strategy, prepared by a BPPT-led multi-stakeholder working group. It covers ethics and policy, talent, infrastructure and data, research and industry innovation, and names five priority areas: health, bureaucratic reform, education and research, food security, and mobility and smart cities. It includes quick wins and a phased implementation roadmap through 2045.
source_publisher: National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN) repository / BPPT Press

title: Surat Edaran Menteri Komunikasi dan Informatika Nomor 9 Tahun 2023 tentang Etika Kecerdasan Artifisial (Circular Letter No. 9 of 2023 on AI Ethics)
short_title: Surat Edaran Menteri Komunikasi dan Informatika Nomor 9 Tahun 2023 tentang Etika Kecerdasan Artifisial
issuing_body: Ministry of Communication and Informatics (now Ministry of Communication and Digital)
summary_plain: A ministerial circular that lays out ethical values for developing and using AI, such as inclusivity, humanity, security, accessibility, transparency, accountability, personal data protection, sustainability and respect for intellectual property. It applies to AI-related businesses and to public and private electronic system operators in Indonesia. It is soft-law guidance intended as a basis for future regulation.

title: The Bletchley Declaration by countries attending the AI Safety Summit, 1–2 November 2023
jurisdiction_name: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
issuing_body: 28 countries and the European Union attending the AI Safety Summit hosted by the United Kingdom
summary_plain: Signed by countries including the United States, China, the EU, India, Japan and Brazil, the declaration recognises the opportunities of AI and the risks of frontier models, commits signatories to cooperate on identifying AI safety risks and building risk-based policies, and launched the summit series continued in Seoul (2024) and Paris (2025) and the network of AI safety institutes.

title: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems (G7, 30 October 2023)
short_title: G7 Hiroshima AI Process code of conduct
jurisdiction_name: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
issuing_body: G7 Leaders (Hiroshima AI Process)
summary_plain: Eleven voluntary actions for organisations developing the most advanced AI systems, including foundation and generative models: risk identification and mitigation across the lifecycle, post-deployment vulnerability and incident monitoring, public transparency reports, responsible information sharing, security controls, content authentication such as watermarking, research on societal risks, priority to global challenges, technical standards, and data-input and personal-data safeguards. It sits alongside the Hiroshima Process guiding principles and, from 2025, an OECD-run voluntary reporting framework.
source_publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan (G7 documents)

title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology – Artificial intelligence – Management system
jurisdiction_name: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
issuing_body: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42
summary_plain: The first certifiable management-system standard for AI. It specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and improving an AI management system within an organisation: context and leadership, AI policy, risk and impact assessment, objectives, resources and competence, operational controls across the AI lifecycle, performance evaluation and improvement, with Annex A controls on data, transparency, human oversight, third parties and responsible use. Certification is voluntary but increasingly requested in procurement; regulators reference it as evidence of governance.

title: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted 22 May 2019 and revised 3 May 2024
jurisdiction_name: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
issuing_body: OECD Council
summary_plain: The first intergovernmental standard on AI. It sets five values-based principles (inclusive growth and well-being; human rights and democratic values including fairness and privacy; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; accountability) and five recommendations to governments (invest in research, foster an inclusive AI ecosystem, enable an agile policy environment, build human capacity and prepare for labour-market transition, cooperate internationally). The 2024 revision updated the definition of an AI system (adopted by the EU AI Act and other laws) and added references to general-purpose and generative AI, misinformation and environmental sustainability. Adherents include all OECD members and several non-members; the G20 AI Principles (2019) draw on it.

title: UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/78/265: Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development (21 March 2024)
short_title: UN General Assembly resolution 78/265 on safe, secure and trustworthy AI
jurisdiction_name: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
issuing_body: United Nations General Assembly
summary_plain: The first General Assembly resolution on AI, adopted by consensus with more than 120 co-sponsors, encourages states to promote safe, secure and trustworthy AI systems that respect human rights and advance the Sustainable Development Goals, to close digital divides, and to develop governance frameworks and interoperable safeguards; it calls on companies to act responsibly. It was followed by resolution A/RES/79/325 (August 2025) establishing an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance under the Global Digital Compact.

title: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (adopted by the General Conference, 23 November 2021)
short_title: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
jurisdiction_name: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
issuing_body: UNESCO General Conference (193 member states)
summary_plain: The first global normative instrument on AI ethics. It sets values (human rights and dignity, environment and ecosystem flourishing, diversity and inclusiveness, peaceful and just societies) and principles (proportionality and do no harm, safety and security, fairness, sustainability, privacy, human oversight, transparency and explainability, responsibility, awareness and literacy, multi-stakeholder governance), and eleven policy action areas from ethical impact assessment and data policy to gender, education, health and the environment. UNESCO supports implementation with a Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) and an Ethical Impact Assessment tool used by dozens of countries.

title: AI – Here for Good: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Ireland (2021, refreshed 2024)
short_title: AI – Here for Good (National AI Strategy)
issuing_body: Government of Ireland (Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment)
summary_plain: Ireland's national AI strategy, first published in July 2021 and refreshed in November 2024 to reflect the EU AI Act and generative AI, is organised around building public trust, leveraging AI for economic and societal benefit, and enablers such as data, infrastructure, skills and governance. The refresh sets out Ireland's AI Act implementation model, public-sector AI guidelines and an AI advisory council.
source_publisher: Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment

title: Israel's Policy on Artificial Intelligence Regulation and Ethics
issuing_body: Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology and Ministry of Justice
summary_plain: Adopted in December 2023 after public consultation, the policy sets Israel's approach: sector-specific regulation by existing regulators, a risk-based approach, preference for soft tools (standards, self-regulation, sandboxes) over binding rules at this stage, alignment with OECD principles, and common ethical principles (growth and sustainable development, human-centricity, equality, transparency, safety, accountability, privacy). It establishes an AI policy coordination centre and an expert advisory forum.
source_publisher: Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology

title: Strategia Italiana per l'Intelligenza Artificiale 2024-2026
issuing_body: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (Department for Digital Transformation) and AgID
summary_plain: The 2024–2026 strategy, drafted by an expert committee for the Department for Digital Transformation and published in July 2024, organises action around research, public administration, enterprises and training, with a foundation-model and compute agenda, an AI foundation to coordinate delivery and a monitoring framework.
source_publisher: Presidenza del Consiglio dei Ministri / AgID

title: Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132 – Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale
issuing_body: Parliament of the Italian Republic
summary_plain: Italy's framework AI law, published in the Official Gazette on 25 September 2025 and in force from 10 October 2025. It states principles (human-centric, transparent, safe AI; protection of fundamental rights), sets sector rules for healthcare (AI as support, not replacement, for clinical decisions), employment (information to workers, an AI-at-work observatory), intellectual professions (client disclosure), justice (judge decides; AI only for organisational support) and public administration, requires parental consent for children under 14, designates AgID and ACN as national authorities, delegates the government to align national law with the EU AI Act, and creates a criminal offence for unlawful dissemination of AI-generated or manipulated content with aggravating circumstances for other crimes committed with AI.
who_it_applies_to: Providers and deployers of AI systems operating in Italy; employers using AI; professionals; healthcare bodies; public administrations; courts; platforms hosting AI-generated content.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy Framework (AI Task Force report)
issuing_body: Government of Jamaica (National AI Task Force)
summary_plain: The task force report proposes a national AI policy with principles for responsible AI, a governance structure, skills and research programmes, public-sector use cases and sector priorities.

title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology (Act No. 53 of 2025)
short_title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology
issuing_body: National Diet of Japan; administered by the Cabinet Office
summary_plain: Japan's first AI-specific statute establishes basic principles and a governmental framework for promoting AI research, development and use. It creates an AI Strategy Headquarters under the Cabinet, requires the government to adopt an AI Basic Plan, and provides for guidelines, information gathering and investigation of cases where AI infringes rights, together with guidance to businesses and the public. Businesses are asked to cooperate with government measures; the Act contains no fines or prohibitions.
source_publisher: Japanese Law Translation Database (Ministry of Justice)

title: AI Guidelines for Business
issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
summary_plain: The AI Guidelines for Business consolidate Japan's previous AI R&D, utilisation and governance guidelines into a single non-binding document addressed to AI developers, providers and business users. They set common guiding principles (such as human-centricity, safety, fairness, privacy, security, transparency and accountability) and describe agile governance practices, with an appendix of practical methods and checklists. The guidelines are updated periodically; version 1.0 was issued in April 2024 and version 1.2 in March 2026.
source_publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry

title: Artificial Intelligence Basic Plan
issuing_body: Cabinet of Japan (Cabinet Office, AI Strategy Headquarters)
summary_plain: The AI Basic Plan is the national strategy required under Article 18 of the 2025 AI Act. It sets basic policies and concrete measures across four areas: accelerating AI deployment, strengthening development capabilities, leading AI governance and building an AI-powered society, with the stated ambition of Japan becoming the most AI-friendly country. The first plan was adopted by Cabinet decision in December 2025 and a revised second plan was adopted in July 2026.

title: Jordanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy and Implementation Roadmap 2023–2027
issuing_body: Government of Jordan (Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship)
summary_plain: Adopted in 2023, the strategy sets priorities on AI governance and ethics, talent and research, adoption in government services and priority sectors, data infrastructure, and international cooperation, with an implementation roadmap and indicators to 2027.

title: Jordanian Charter of Artificial Intelligence Ethics
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship
summary_plain: The charter sets ethical principles for the development and use of AI in Jordan, including human dignity, fairness, transparency, accountability, safety, privacy and sustainability, addressed to public and private organisations.

title: Концепция развития искусственного интеллекта на 2024–2029 годы
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary_plain: Approved by government decree in July 2024, the concept sets targets for AI infrastructure (supercomputing, data), talent, adoption in the public sector and economy, a national AI platform and regulatory development that led to the 2025 AI law.

title: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan "On Artificial Intelligence" (signed November 2025)
issuing_body: Parliament of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary_plain: The law defines AI systems and their classification by level of autonomy and risk, sets principles (legality, fairness, transparency, safety, human control), assigns duties to owners and operators of AI systems including risk management, labelling of AI-generated content and protection of personal data, prohibits certain manipulative and social-scoring uses, provides for a national AI platform and state support measures, and allocates state regulation to the authorised body.

title: Kenya Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2030
issuing_body: Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy (MICDE)
summary_plain: Kenya's first national AI strategy sets a five-year agenda built on three pillars: AI digital infrastructure, data and AI governance, and AI research, innovation and commercialisation. It aligns with the Kenya National Digital Masterplan 2022-2032 and priorities sectors such as agriculture, health and education. A separate implementation roadmap was later published by the ministry.
source_publisher: Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy

title: Kuwait National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2028
issuing_body: Government of Kuwait (CAIT)
summary_plain: The strategy sets objectives on AI in government services, national talent, data and cloud infrastructure, ethical and responsible AI, and partnerships, aligned with Kuwait Vision 2035.

title: Informatīvais ziņojums "Par mākslīgā intelekta risinājumu attīstību"
issuing_body: Cabinet of Ministers of Latvia
summary_plain: The 2020 informational report approved by the Cabinet sets Latvia's direction on AI: public-sector use cases, data availability, skills, research and ethical principles, later carried into the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021–2027.

title: Lebanon National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024–2030
issuing_body: Government of Lebanon (OMSAR)
summary_plain: The strategy sets objectives for AI governance and ethics, talent and research, adoption in public services and the economy, and data infrastructure, drawing on UNESCO's readiness assessment.

title: Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy: A vision of the future
issuing_body: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation
summary_plain: Published in 2019, the strategy sets a vision for AI in Lithuania across research, industry, public sector, skills and ethics, and proposes a coordination structure and funding measures.

title: Artificial Intelligence: a strategic vision for Luxembourg
short_title: AI: a strategic vision for Luxembourg (2019)
issuing_body: Government of Luxembourg (Ministry of Digitalisation)
summary_plain: Published in May 2019, the vision positions Luxembourg as a living lab for applied AI with priorities on skills, data and infrastructure, public-sector use, research and trustworthy, human-centric AI.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill (proposed)
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital / National AI Office (NAIO)
summary_plain: A proposed horizontal AI law announced for stakeholder engagement and public consultation by the Ministry of Digital through the National AI Office. It takes a risk-based approach across the AI lifecycle, assigns responsibilities according to actors' roles, and is intended to complement existing laws rather than regulate AI outputs directly. It encourages incident reporting, safeguards and sandboxes, and the government aims to table it in Parliament.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2021-2025 (AI-Rmap)
issuing_body: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
summary_plain: Malaysia's five-year AI roadmap developed by MOSTI through a quadruple-helix consultation. It sets strategic thrusts on governance, R&D, infrastructure, talent and adoption, and identifies national use cases in five priority sectors: agriculture and forestry, healthcare, smart cities and transport, education and public services. It is guided by responsible AI principles including fairness, transparency, accountability and privacy.
source_publisher: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, Malaysia

title: The National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics (AIGE)
short_title: The National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics
issuing_body: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
summary_plain: Voluntary national guidelines that set out seven principles for responsible AI: fairness; reliability, safety and control; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability; and human-centricity. They give tailored guidance to end users, policymakers and AI developers and are meant to build public trust and reduce ethical risks while supporting adoption.
source_publisher: Malaysian Science, Technology Information Centre (MASTIC), MOSTI

title: Malta: The Ultimate AI Launchpad – A Strategy and Vision for Artificial Intelligence in Malta 2030
issuing_body: Government of Malta (Parliamentary Secretariat for Financial Services, Digital Economy and Innovation)
summary_plain: Launched in October 2019, the strategy sets three pillars (investment and adoption, public-sector adoption, private-sector adoption) and enablers (education, legal and ethical framework, ecosystem infrastructure), including an ethical AI framework and the MDIA's voluntary AI certification.

title: Mauritius Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Government of Mauritius (Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation)
summary_plain: Published in November 2018, the strategy identifies AI applications in manufacturing, health, fintech, agriculture, ocean economy and public services, proposes a Mauritius AI Council, skills programmes and data policies, and addresses ethics and regulation.

title: Iniciativa con proyecto de decreto por el que se expide la Ley Federal para el Desarrollo Ético, Soberano e Inclusivo de la Inteligencia Artificial (Initiative to enact the Federal Law for the Ethical, Sovereign and Inclusive Development of Artificial…
short_title: Iniciativa con proyecto de decreto por el que se expide la Ley Federal para el Desarrollo Ético, Soberano e Inclusivo de
issuing_body: Cámara de Diputados (LXVI Legislatura) – deputies of Morena and PVEM
summary_plain: This initiative, signed by a bloc of Morena and PVEM deputies and published in the Gaceta Parlamentaria on 30 April 2025, would create Mexico's first general federal AI law. It proposes principles of legality, transparency, human oversight and precaution, a risk 'traffic light' classification with prohibited uses, a National AI Council and an algorithmic audit platform. It was referred to committee and remains under consideration in Congress.
source_publisher: Sistema de Información Legislativa, Secretaría de Gobernación

title: Plan Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (National Artificial Intelligence Plan)
issuing_body: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (ATDT)
summary_plain: Mexico's National AI Plan, prepared by the ATDT and presented in April 2026, organises federal AI efforts around three pillars: an ethical and legal framework, talent and public software, and strategic compute infrastructure. It includes a public AI training centre aiming to certify tens of thousands of people, a government 'Fábrica de IA' developing solutions for public services, and the Coatlicue supercomputer, with 2026 milestones and 2030 targets for citizen-facing AI services.
source_publisher: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (gob.mx)

title: Mongolia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Government of Mongolia
summary_plain: The strategy sets goals for AI in public services, the economy, education and research, data and infrastructure, and ethical AI governance.

title: Maroc Digital 2030: national digital strategy with an artificial intelligence pillar
issuing_body: Government of Morocco (Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform)
summary_plain: Launched in September 2024, Digital Morocco 2030 sets targets for digital public services, the digital economy and talent, with an AI component covering a national AI centre, sovereign compute and data, sector use cases and governance, and announces a national AI strategy and legal framework.
source_publisher: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform

title: Namibia National Artificial Intelligence Policy
issuing_body: Government of Namibia
summary_plain: A national AI policy under development following the Fourth Industrial Revolution task-force report, covering governance, skills, public-sector use and data.

title: Concept Paper on the Use and Practice of Artificial Intelligence in Nepal
short_title: Concept Paper on the Use and Practice of Artificial Intelligence in Nepal
issuing_body: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
summary_plain: A concept paper prepared by a ministry-appointed committee that surveys the state of AI use in Nepal, its opportunities and risks, and the gaps in existing law and infrastructure. It recommends formulating a national AI policy and strategy, addressing data protection, privacy and cybersecurity, and building governance structures. The paper was published for public suggestions and is cited in the 2025 policy as its precursor.
source_publisher: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, Government of Nepal

title: Individual Privacy Act, 2075 (2018) — Nepal
issuing_body: Federal Parliament of Nepal
summary_plain: The Individual Privacy Act 2075 gives effect to the constitutional right to privacy in Nepal. It regulates the collection, storage, processing, use and disclosure of personal information by public bodies and private entities, requires consent for collection and use of personal data subject to exceptions, restricts sensitive data, and provides remedies and penalties. It is the main binding law affecting AI systems that process personal data in Nepal. The Individual Privacy Regulation 2077 (2020) provides implementing rules.
who_it_applies_to: Any organisation collecting or processing personal information of individuals in Nepal.
source_reference: Document-level URL and section references to be added by reviewer

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy, 2082 (2025) — Nepal
issuing_body: Government of Nepal, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
summary_plain: Nepal's National AI Policy sets the government's direction for developing and using artificial intelligence. Based on the published summaries, it aims to build AI infrastructure and skills, promote ethical and responsible AI, strengthen data governance, establish institutional arrangements for AI oversight, and prepare legal and regulatory measures. It is a policy framework, not a law, and does not itself create enforceable obligations on private organisations.
who_it_applies_to: Government of Nepal bodies (primary); AI developers and deployers in Nepal through future rules.
source_publisher: Government of Nepal, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
source_reference: Document-level URL to be added by reviewer

title: Algoritmeregister van de Nederlandse overheid (Government Algorithm Register)
issuing_body: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations
summary_plain: A public register in which Dutch government organisations describe the algorithms they use that affect citizens: purpose, legal basis, data, human oversight, risks and contact points. Launched in December 2022 and extended since, it aims to make automated decision-making by government transparent and contestable. Ministries were asked to publish all impactful and high-risk algorithms.
source_publisher: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations

title: Overheidsbrede visie generatieve AI (Government-wide vision on generative AI)
issuing_body: Government of the Netherlands (Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations)
summary_plain: Adopted in January 2024, the vision sets the government's position on generative AI: a human-centric, safe and fair approach, provisional restrictions on using non-contracted generative AI tools with government data, investment in Dutch and European open models (GPT-NL), and actions on skills, procurement and supervision. It complements the AI Act and the government's AI strategy.

title: New Zealand's Strategy for Artificial Intelligence: Investing with Confidence
issuing_body: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
summary_plain: Published in July 2025, the strategy aims to lift AI adoption by businesses, especially small and medium enterprises, and the public sector, by reducing barriers, providing clear guidance (Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses), building skills and pursuing a light-touch, proportionate regulatory approach that relies on existing law and international alignment (OECD principles). It rules out a standalone AI act for now.

title: Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand (2020)
short_title: Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand
issuing_body: Stats NZ (Government Chief Data Steward) on behalf of signatory agencies
summary_plain: Launched in July 2020, the charter commits signatory government agencies to transparency (plain-English explanations of how algorithms are used), partnership with Māori (Te Tiriti), people-focused use, data fit for purpose, privacy, ethics and human rights safeguards, human oversight and channels for challenge, applied through a risk matrix for high-impact algorithms. Around 30 agencies have signed; a 2021 review recommended stronger implementation.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy (FMCIDE) with NITDA / NCAIR
summary_plain: The draft strategy sets out Nigeria's vision for AI across five pillars: infrastructure, a thriving AI ecosystem, sectoral adoption, responsible and ethical AI, and governance. It was co-created through a 2024 multi-stakeholder workshop convened by the ministry and includes an implementation roadmap with pilot projects and KPIs. The published document on the NCAIR site is marked as a draft dated August 2024.
source_publisher: National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (NITDA)

title: Nasjonal strategi for kunstig intelligens (National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence)
issuing_body: Norwegian Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation
summary_plain: Published in January 2020, the strategy sets ethical principles for AI in Norway based on the EU High-Level Expert Group guidelines, and measures on data access and sharing, language resources, research, skills, public-sector and business adoption, security and the Data Protection Authority's sandbox.

title: National Programme for Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Digital Technologies; AI policy for government entities
short_title: National AI programme and government AI policy (2024)
issuing_body: Government of Oman (MTCIT)
summary_plain: The programme sets AI adoption goals for government and priority sectors, talent and research initiatives and an AI policy with ethical principles and governance requirements for government entities.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy 2025
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication (approved by the Federal Cabinet)
summary_plain: Pakistan's first national AI policy, organised around six pillars: innovation ecosystem, awareness and readiness, secure AI, transformation of sectors, AI infrastructure, and international partnerships. It proposes a National AI Fund drawn from Ignite's R&D fund, centres of excellence, venture and innovation funds, regulatory sandboxes and KPIs, with an AI Council to oversee delivery. Targets include large-scale training of AI professionals and funded research projects.
source_publisher: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, Government of Pakistan

title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial de Panamá
issuing_body: Government of Panama (AIG)
summary_plain: Panama has been developing a national AI strategy with UNESCO support, covering governance and ethics, public-sector adoption, talent, data infrastructure and the logistics and financial sectors.

title: Política Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Paraguay
issuing_body: Government of Paraguay (MITIC)
summary_plain: Presented in 2024, the policy sets objectives on ethical and human-centred AI, capacity building, public-sector adoption, data and infrastructure, and research, aligned with the UNESCO recommendation.

title: Decreto Supremo N° 115-2025-PCM – Reglamento de la Ley N° 31814 (Supreme Decree No. 115-2025-PCM – Regulation of Law No. 31814)
issuing_body: Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM)
summary_plain: This regulation, published on 9 September 2025, develops Law 31814 with six titles and 36 articles. It introduces a risk classification distinguishing prohibited uses, high-risk systems and acceptable-risk systems, sets transparency, data protection and governance obligations for public and private actors, and provides for sandboxes, capacity-building and reporting channels. Compliance is phased in over one to four years depending on the sector and type of organisation.

title: Ley N° 31814 – Ley que promueve el uso de la inteligencia artificial en favor del desarrollo económico y social del país (Law No. 31814 – Law promoting the use of artificial intelligence for the country's economic and social development)
issuing_body: Congreso de la República; implemented by the Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM)
summary_plain: Law 31814, promulgated on 4 July 2023 and published on 5 July 2023, declares AI development of national interest and frames its use within Peru's digital transformation process. It sets principles such as risk-based safety, ethics, transparency and multi-stakeholder participation, and designates the PCM's digital government secretariat as the national AI authority. The law is promotional in character and left detailed obligations to a later regulation.

title: National AI Strategy for the Philippines (NAIS-PH)
short_title: National AI Strategy for the Philippines
issuing_body: Department of Science and Technology (DOST)
summary_plain: A national AI strategy proposed by DOST at National Innovation Day 2025, structured around five core strategies: infrastructure, workforce, innovation, ethics and policy, and deployment, phased from 2024 to 2028. It includes a national high-performance computing centre, AI micro-credentials and an AI hub linking regional industries to solutions, coordinated with DICT, DepEd, CHED, TESDA, DTI and others. DOST later launched NAICRI as its institutional backbone.
source_publisher: Department of Science and Technology, Philippines

title: National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0 (NAISR 2.0)
issuing_body: Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
summary_plain: An updated national AI roadmap launched by DTI together with the Center for AI Research, building on the 2021 roadmap and adding generative AI. It aims to strengthen entrepreneurship and competitiveness, improve public services, support responsible governance of AI and identify investment and R&D priorities. CAIR is intended to serve as a national AI research hub for industry-relevant solutions.
source_publisher: Department of Trade and Industry, Philippines

title: Projekt ustawy o systemach sztucznej inteligencji
short_title: Draft act on AI systems (AI Act implementation)
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital Affairs
summary_plain: The draft act implements the EU AI Act in Poland: it creates the Commission for the Development and Safety of Artificial Intelligence as the market-surveillance authority and single point of contact, sets procedures for complaints and inspections, provides for a regulatory sandbox and defines the national penalty regime.

title: Polityka dla rozwoju sztucznej inteligencji w Polsce od roku 2020
short_title: Policy for the development of AI in Poland (2020)
issuing_body: Council of Ministers of Poland
