summary_plain: Adopted by resolution of the Council of Ministers in December 2020, the policy sets goals for AI in society, business, science, education, international cooperation and the public sector, with short-, medium- and long-term actions and an ethics and trustworthy-AI dimension.

title: AI Portugal 2030: Portuguese National Initiative on Digital Skills – Artificial Intelligence strategy
issuing_body: Government of Portugal (INCoDe.2030)
summary_plain: Published in 2019 under the INCoDe.2030 initiative, AI Portugal 2030 sets objectives for research, skills, public administration, industry adoption and international positioning, with priority application areas such as natural language, mobility, energy and health, and a commitment to ethical and trustworthy AI.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Qatar 2019
short_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Qatar 2019
issuing_body: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (formerly Ministry of Transport and Communications)
summary_plain: Developed by the Qatar Center for Artificial Intelligence and adopted by the government as the national strategy, the document sets out six pillars: education, data access, employment, business, research, and ethics. It provides recommendations for building an AI research and innovation ecosystem and for the responsible adoption of AI across society. A national AI committee was subsequently formed to develop an implementation plan.
source_publisher: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, Qatar

title: Strategia Națională în domeniul Inteligenței Artificiale 2024–2027
issuing_body: Government of Romania
summary_plain: Approved by government decision in July 2024, the strategy sets objectives on infrastructure and data, research and innovation, skills, public-sector and business adoption, and governance and ethics aligned with the EU AI Act, with an action plan and monitoring indicators.
source_publisher: Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalisation

title: Federal Law No. 123-FZ of 24 April 2020 on an experiment to establish special regulation to create the conditions for the development and implementation of AI technologies in Moscow
issuing_body: Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation
summary_plain: Establishes a five-year experimental legal regime in Moscow (from 1 July 2020) allowing participants to develop and deploy AI technologies under special rules, including processing of anonymised personal data for AI purposes, coordinated by the Moscow government with a register of participants. It was accompanied by amendments to the personal-data law.

title: Национальная стратегия развития искусственного интеллекта на период до 2030 года (Presidential Decree No. 490 of 10 October 2019, as amended by Decree No. 124 of 15 February 2024)
issuing_body: President of the Russian Federation
summary_plain: The national strategy sets goals for AI research, compute, data, talent and adoption across the economy and public administration to 2030, with the 2024 amendment adding targets on domestic compute capacity, large generative models, share of organisations using AI, and trusted-AI requirements for the public sector. It is implemented through the federal "Artificial Intelligence" project.

title: The National AI Policy
issuing_body: Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT) with Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA)
summary_plain: Rwanda's national AI policy sets out six policy areas and fourteen recommendations covering skills and literacy, infrastructure, data, responsible AI governance, public-sector adoption and ecosystem development. It proposes a Responsible AI Office housed in MINICT to drive an implementation plan and monitor progress. Priority sectors include health, agriculture, education, finance and public services.
source_publisher: Ministry of ICT and Innovation, Republic of Rwanda

title: AI Ethics Principles
issuing_body: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
summary_plain: SDAIA's AI Ethics Principles set out ethical principles and associated controls for entities developing, deploying or affected by AI systems in Saudi Arabia, covering fairness, privacy and security, humanity, social and environmental benefit, reliability and safety, transparency, and accountability. The document assigns roles and responsibilities and marks certain controls as binding for public entities. The 2025 edition updates the September 2023 version 1.0.
source_publisher: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority

title: National Strategy for Data & AI
issuing_body: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
summary_plain: The national strategy, approved by royal decision in July 2020, sets an ambition for Saudi Arabia to be among the leading data- and AI-driven economies through phased milestones to 2030. It targets talent development, welcoming regulation, investment attraction, research and an active ecosystem, with measurable goals such as training data and AI specialists, attracting investment and creating startups.
source_publisher: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle du Sénégal
issuing_body: Government of Senegal
summary_plain: The strategy sets priorities on AI for public services, agriculture, health and education, talent and research, data and infrastructure, and ethical governance, within the New Technological Deal.

title: Стратегија развоја вештачке интелигенције у Републици Србији за период 2025–2030
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Serbia
summary_plain: Adopted in 2025, the second national AI strategy sets goals to 2030 on research and talent, AI in the economy and public administration, data and compute infrastructure, trustworthy AI and alignment with the EU AI Act and the Council of Europe convention, and the preparation of an AI law.
source_publisher: Government of the Republic of Serbia

title: Етичке смернице за развој, примену и употребу поуздане и одговорне вештачке интелигенције
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Serbia
summary_plain: Adopted in March 2023, the guidelines set principles and requirements for trustworthy and responsible AI in Serbia (human agency, safety, privacy, transparency, non-discrimination, societal well-being, accountability), with self-assessment questions for developers and users, drawing on the EU ethics guidelines and the UNESCO recommendation.
source_publisher: Government of the Republic of Serbia

title: Sierra Leone National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Government of Sierra Leone
summary_plain: The strategy sets priorities on AI in public services, health, agriculture and education, skills and research, data infrastructure and ethical governance.

title: Model AI Governance Framework (Second Edition) and Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
issuing_body: Infocomm Media Development Authority and Personal Data Protection Commission; AI Verify Foundation (generative AI edition)
summary_plain: Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework is a voluntary, sector-agnostic guide for organisations deploying AI. The second edition (January 2020) covers four areas: internal governance structures and measures, determining the level of human involvement in AI-augmented decision-making, operations management (data, model development, monitoring), and stakeholder interaction and communication. The May 2024 Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI extends it with nine dimensions including accountability, data, trusted development and deployment, incident reporting, testing and assurance, security, content provenance, safety and alignment research, and AI for the public good.
who_it_applies_to: Organisations deploying AI (any sector), and developers of generative AI models and applications.
source_publisher: Personal Data Protection Commission Singapore and IMDA

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2.0 (NAIS 2.0)
issuing_body: Smart Nation Group / Ministry of Digital Development and Information
summary_plain: Singapore's second national AI strategy, launched under the banner of AI for the public good. It sets goals of excellence and empowerment and organises work across three systems, ten enablers and fifteen actions covering talent, compute, data, industry adoption, research and governance. A 2026 update set ten refreshed priorities and launched sector AI Missions under the new National AI Council.

title: PDPC Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems
issuing_body: Personal Data Protection Commission Singapore
summary_plain: These advisory guidelines explain how the Personal Data Protection Act applies when organisations use personal data to develop, test and deploy AI systems that make recommendations, predictions or decisions. They clarify the consent obligation and relevant exceptions (business improvement and research), what to include in notifications to individuals, accountability practices such as documenting data provenance and model development, and expectations for service providers building bespoke AI systems.
who_it_applies_to: PDPA-regulated organisations and their AI service providers.

title: Národná stratégia pre umelú inteligenciu 2030
issuing_body: Government of Slovakia (MIRRI)
summary_plain: The strategy to 2030 sets objectives for AI research, skills, data and infrastructure, adoption in public administration and industry, and trustworthy AI aligned with the EU AI Act.

title: Nacionalni program spodbujanja razvoja in uporabe umetne inteligence v Republiki Sloveniji do leta 2025
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Slovenia
summary_plain: Adopted in May 2021, the programme sets measures on research and innovation, skills, data and infrastructure, public-sector and business adoption, ethics and trustworthy AI, and international cooperation, including support for the UNESCO IRCAI centre.

title: Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy
short_title: Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Department of Communications and Digital Technologies (DCDT)
summary_plain: Approved by Cabinet in March/April 2026 and gazetted for a 60-day comment period, the draft policy proposed guiding principles, institutional arrangements and implementation pathways for AI across the public and private sectors, building on the department's 2024 National AI Policy Framework. The Minister announced its withdrawal on 26 April 2026 after fictitious citations were found in its reference list, and the withdrawal was formally gazetted in June 2026.

title: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of a Foundation for Trust (AI Basic Act, Act No. 20676)
issuing_body: National Assembly of the Republic of Korea; competent ministry Ministry of Science and ICT
summary_plain: Korea's AI Basic Act is a comprehensive framework statute combining industrial promotion with trust and safety rules. It gives a legal basis for a national AI master plan every three years and the National AI Committee, supports R&D, data, standardisation and SMEs, and imposes duties on operators of high-impact AI (risk management, explanation, human oversight) and transparency duties to notify users of generative AI output. Foreign operators above a threshold must designate a domestic representative. It was promulgated in January 2025 and took effect on 22 January 2026 after a one-year grace period.
source_publisher: Korea Ministry of Government Legislation, National Law Information Center

title: Anteproyecto de Ley para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial
short_title: Draft law on good use and governance of AI
issuing_body: Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service
summary_plain: The draft implements the EU AI Act in Spain: it allocates supervision among AESIA, the data-protection authority, the electoral board, the financial and audiovisual regulators, sets the national penalty scale (up to EUR 35 million or 7% of turnover for prohibited practices), treats failure to label AI-generated content as a serious infringement and provides for the national sandbox to continue.
source_publisher: Agencia Española de Supervisión de la Inteligencia Artificial

title: Real Decreto 729/2023, de 22 de agosto, por el que se aprueba el Estatuto de la Agencia Española de Supervisión de Inteligencia Artificial
issuing_body: Government of Spain
summary_plain: Creates and organises AESIA, the Spanish AI Supervision Agency, as a public body attached to the Ministry for Digital Transformation. AESIA supervises and inspects AI systems, promotes sandboxes and standards, and acts as national authority for the EU AI Act. The decree sets its governance, functions and funding.

title: Real Decreto 817/2023, de 8 de noviembre, que establece un entorno controlado de pruebas para el ensayo del cumplimiento de la propuesta de Reglamento de IA
issuing_body: Government of Spain
summary_plain: Establishes Spain's controlled testing environment (sandbox) for providers of high-risk AI systems to test compliance with the then-proposed EU AI Act requirements: risk management, data governance, documentation, transparency, human oversight, accuracy and robustness. Participation is voluntary; participants receive guidance and produce documentation that feeds into national implementation.

title: National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence for Sri Lanka
issuing_body: Government of Sri Lanka (Ministry of Digital Economy)
summary_plain: The strategy sets priorities on AI skills and research, public-sector and industry adoption, data and compute infrastructure, and responsible-AI governance, with a national AI centre and implementation task force.

title: Färdplan för Sverige – AI-kommissionens slutbetänkande (SOU 2024:94)
issuing_body: AI Commission appointed by the Government of Sweden
summary_plain: The government-appointed AI Commission's final report sets out a roadmap for Sweden with around 75 proposals: a national AI task force and data factory, compute and skills investment, AI in public administration and health care, access to data for research and innovation, and measures to make the most of the EU AI Act. It estimates costs and proposes a funding envelope over several years.

title: Federal Council decision on the regulation of artificial intelligence: ratification of the Council of Europe Convention and sector-specific adjustments
issuing_body: Swiss Federal Council
summary_plain: On 12 February 2025 the Federal Council decided how Switzerland will regulate AI: it will ratify the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI and implement it mainly through targeted changes to existing law where needed (for example transparency, data protection and non-discrimination), avoid a horizontal AI act, and complement legislation with non-binding measures such as self-regulation and agreements with industry. Federal departments were tasked to prepare a consultation draft by the end of 2026.

title: Leitlinien "Künstliche Intelligenz" für den Bund
short_title: Guidelines on AI for the Federal Administration (2020)
issuing_body: Swiss Federal Council
summary_plain: Adopted in November 2020, seven guidelines steer the use of AI by the federal administration: putting people at the centre, conditions for development and use, transparency and explainability, accountability, security, active participation in AI governance, and involvement of stakeholders.

title: 人工智慧基本法 (Artificial Intelligence Basic Act) – draft approved by the Executive Yuan, July 2024
issuing_body: Executive Yuan of Taiwan (National Science and Technology Council)
summary_plain: A framework act setting seven principles for AI development and use, requiring the government to promote AI research, talent and infrastructure, to establish a risk-classification framework and safety standards, to protect personal data, labour and consumers, to provide for liability, disclosure of AI-generated content and non-discrimination, and to designate competent authorities by sector, with the NSTC coordinating.

title: Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Tajikistan for the period up to 2040
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Tajikistan
summary_plain: Approved by government decree in 2021, the strategy sets long-term goals for AI research, education, infrastructure and use in the economy and public administration to 2040.

title: Tanzania National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Government of Tanzania
summary_plain: A national AI strategy under development covering governance and ethics, skills, public-sector and agricultural use cases, data and infrastructure.

title: (Draft) Principles of the Law on Artificial Intelligence
short_title: (Draft) Principles of the Law on Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society / Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA)
summary_plain: Draft principles for a Thai AI law released for public hearing by MDES and ETDA. They propose a risk-based structure that distinguishes prohibited and high-risk AI, duties for providers and deployers, human oversight, incident reporting and a regulatory sandbox, while leaving sector regulators to set proportionate rules. The draft merges the 2022 ONDE royal decree draft and the 2023 ETDA promotion act draft.

title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022-2027)
short_title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan
issuing_body: Cabinet of Thailand (prepared by MHESI and MDES; NECTEC/NSTDA secretariat)
summary_plain: A cabinet-approved strategy and action plan with five strategies: readiness in ethics, law and regulation; national AI infrastructure; human capability and education; AI technology and innovation development; and promotion of AI use in public and private sectors. It sets targets for AI talent, research prototypes and economic impact through 2027 and is implemented in phases coordinated across ministries.
source_publisher: National Electronics and Computer Technology Center (NECTEC), NSTDA

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle de la Tunisie
issuing_body: Government of Tunisia (Ministry of Communication Technologies)
summary_plain: The strategy sets objectives on AI talent and research, adoption in public services and the economy, data and infrastructure, start-up support and ethical governance.

title: Yapay Zekâ Kanunu Teklifi (Artificial Intelligence Law proposal submitted to the Grand National Assembly, June 2024)
issuing_body: Grand National Assembly of Türkiye (private member's bill)
summary_plain: A short framework bill proposing principles for AI (safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, privacy), a risk-based approach with registration of high-risk systems, operator obligations and penalties, and supervision by designated authorities, broadly modelled on the EU AI Act.
source_publisher: Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye

title: Ulusal Yapay Zekâ Stratejisi 2021–2025 (National Artificial Intelligence Strategy)
issuing_body: Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye (Digital Transformation Office) and Ministry of Industry and Technology
summary_plain: Published by Presidential Circular in August 2021, the strategy sets six priorities: training AI experts and increasing employment, supporting research and innovation, access to quality data and technical infrastructure, regulations to accelerate socio-economic adaptation, strengthening international cooperation, and accelerating structural and workforce transformation. Its action plan was updated for 2024–2025.

title: UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031
issuing_body: UAE Government, Office of the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence
summary_plain: The UAE National Strategy for AI 2031 aims to position the UAE as a global leader in AI by 2031. It sets objectives across priority sectors, AI talent and research, data and infrastructure, government adoption and governance, including a commitment to AI ethics and to developing appropriate regulation. It is a strategy document that guides government programmes and does not itself impose obligations on private organisations.
who_it_applies_to: UAE government entities (primary); AI companies and partners engaging with government (indirect).
source_reference: Document-level URL to be added by reviewer

title: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (UAE PDPL)
issuing_body: UAE Federal Government
summary_plain: The UAE Personal Data Protection Law is the federal data-protection law applying outside the DIFC and ADGM free zones. It sets principles for lawful processing, consent and its exceptions, data-subject rights (including the right to object to automated decision-making without human intervention), controller and processor duties, security and breach notification to the UAE Data Office, cross-border transfer rules, and data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing including new technologies.
who_it_applies_to: Organisations processing personal data of individuals in the UAE, including AI developers and deployers using such data.
source_reference: Article numbers to be added by reviewer

title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
short_title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: UAE Cabinet / Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
summary_plain: A twelve-principle charter approved by the UAE Cabinet setting expectations for AI development and use, including safety, algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, human oversight, governance and accountability, and compliance with applicable laws and treaties. It is a guiding framework rather than binding legislation and supports the objectives of the UAE Strategy for AI.
source_publisher: Official Platform of the UAE Government (u.ae)

title: UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (UAE National Strategy for AI 2031)
issuing_body: UAE Government / Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence
summary_plain: Launched in October 2017, the strategy aims to embed AI across government services and priority sectors such as health, education, transport, energy and space, and to make the UAE a leading AI destination by 2031. Its objectives include AI-friendly legislation, talent development, research capability, data infrastructure and strong governance. The UAE Council for AI was created to drive implementation.
source_publisher: Official Platform of the UAE Government (u.ae)

title: Uganda National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Government of Uganda (Ministry of ICT and National Guidance)
summary_plain: A national AI strategy under development covering governance and ethics, skills, public-sector and agricultural use cases, data and infrastructure, within the Digital Transformation Roadmap.

title: AI Opportunities Action Plan
issuing_body: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
summary_plain: The AI Opportunities Action Plan is an independent report by Matt Clifford commissioned by the government, containing 50 recommendations organised under three aims: laying foundations (compute, data, skills and regulation), driving AI adoption across the public and private sectors, and securing homegrown frontier AI capability. The government published a response accepting the recommendations and treats the plan as its roadmap for AI-led growth.
source_publisher: GOV.UK (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)

title: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (white paper and government response)
issuing_body: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
summary_plain: The UK white paper sets out a principles-based, context-specific approach to regulating AI. Instead of a single AI law, it asks existing regulators to interpret and apply five cross-cutting principles within their remits: safety, security and robustness; appropriate transparency and explainability; fairness; accountability and governance; and contestability and redress. Central government provides coordination, monitoring and guidance.
who_it_applies_to: UK regulators (primary audience), and indirectly any organisation whose AI use falls within a regulator's remit.
source_publisher: UK Government, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
short_title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
issuing_body: Government Digital Service (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)
summary_plain: The AI Playbook is official guidance for UK public-sector organisations on selecting, buying, building and deploying AI. It sets ten principles covering legality, security, human oversight, transparency and accountability, and explains AI capabilities, limitations and risks in plain terms. It expands and replaces the January 2024 Generative AI Framework for HMG to cover a broader range of AI technologies.

title: ICO Guidance on AI and data protection
issuing_body: Information Commissioner's Office
summary_plain: The ICO's guidance explains how UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply when organisations develop or use AI that processes personal data. It covers accountability and governance, lawfulness and fairness, transparency, data minimisation, security, individual rights, and automated decision-making. The guidance is not itself law, but it reflects how the regulator interprets binding obligations and is the reference point in ICO enforcement.
who_it_applies_to: Controllers and processors under UK GDPR, including developers and deployers of AI.

title: Roadmap for the regulation of artificial intelligence in Ukraine
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
summary_plain: Published in October 2023, the roadmap sets a two-stage, bottom-up approach: first voluntary instruments (white paper, general and sector recommendations, a self-assessment tool, a code of conduct and regulatory sandboxes) to help businesses prepare, then a law on AI harmonised with the EU AI Act, timed with Ukraine's EU accession path.

title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Uruguay 2024-2030 (National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Uruguay 2024-2030)
short_title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Uruguay 2024-2030
issuing_body: Agencia de Gobierno Electrónico y Sociedad de la Información y del Conocimiento (Agesic)
summary_plain: Uruguay's 2024-2030 strategy was approved on 21 November 2024 by the public-sector Strategic Committee for AI and Data after a participatory process involving more than 300 people from state bodies, civil society and the private sector, with technical support from CAF and UNESCO. It sets guiding principles and three objectives: governance and safeguards for ethical and safe AI, national capabilities in infrastructure, data and talent, and use of AI for sustainable development and better public services. A roadmap with goals and semi-annual reporting accompanies the strategy.

title: California SB 53: Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act
issuing_body: California State Legislature
summary_plain: SB 53 requires "large frontier developers" (developers of the most compute-intensive models above statutory thresholds) to publish a frontier AI framework describing how they assess and mitigate catastrophic risks, publish transparency reports when deploying new frontier models, report critical safety incidents to the California Office of Emergency Services, and protect employees who report safety concerns. It also directs creation of a public computing cluster ("CalCompute").
who_it_applies_to: Frontier-model developers operating in California, including companies based elsewhere that train frontier models and do business in the state.
source_reference: Chapter 853, Statutes of 2025 (reviewer to confirm chapter number)

title: Colorado Senate Bill 24-205: Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence (Colorado AI Act)
issuing_body: Colorado General Assembly
summary_plain: The Colorado AI Act requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination. High-risk systems are those that make, or are a substantial factor in making, consequential decisions about education, employment, financial or lending services, essential government services, healthcare, housing, insurance or legal services. Deployers must run risk-management programmes and impact assessments, notify consumers, and explain adverse decisions; developers must document systems and disclose known risks.
who_it_applies_to: Developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems used to make consequential decisions about Colorado residents.

title: Illinois Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act (820 ILCS 42)
issuing_body: Illinois General Assembly
summary_plain: In force since 1 January 2020, the Act requires employers that use AI to analyse video interviews of applicants for Illinois-based positions to notify applicants, explain how the AI works and what characteristics it evaluates, obtain consent, limit sharing of videos, and delete videos on request within 30 days; a 2022 amendment requires employers relying solely on AI to decide who gets an in-person interview to report demographic data annually.

title: Illinois Public Act 103-0804 (HB 3773): Artificial intelligence in employment decisions – amendment to the Illinois Human Rights Act
short_title: Illinois HB 3773 (AI in employment, Human Rights Act amendment)
issuing_body: Illinois General Assembly
summary_plain: Signed 9 August 2024 and effective 1 January 2026, the Act makes it a civil-rights violation for an employer to use artificial intelligence in recruitment, hiring, promotion, discipline, discharge or other terms of employment in a way that subjects employees to discrimination on the basis of protected classes, or to use zip codes as a proxy for protected classes. Employers must notify employees when AI is used for such decisions; the Department of Human Rights is to adopt rules on notice.

title: New York City Local Law 144 of 2021 on Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDT) and DCWP implementing rules
short_title: NYC Local Law 144 (automated employment decision tools)
issuing_body: New York City Council; rules by the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
summary_plain: Employers and employment agencies may not use an automated employment decision tool to screen candidates or employees for hiring or promotion in New York City unless the tool has had an independent bias audit within the past year, a summary of the audit results is published, and candidates receive at least ten business days' notice of the tool's use, the job qualifications assessed, and how to request an alternative process or accommodation. The bias audit calculates selection and scoring impact ratios by sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories. Enforcement began 5 July 2023.
source_publisher: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection

title: New York Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act (S.6953-B / A.6453-B, signed December 2025)
short_title: New York RAISE Act (frontier model safety)
issuing_body: New York State Legislature
summary_plain: The RAISE Act requires large developers of frontier AI models (defined by training compute and revenue thresholds) to publish and follow a safety and security protocol, report critical safety incidents to the state within a set period, not deploy models that create unreasonable risk of critical harm, and submit to Attorney General enforcement with civil penalties; the chapter amendments create a state oversight office and align definitions with California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act.

title: Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security (ELVIS) Act of 2024 (Tennessee Public Chapter 588)
issuing_body: Tennessee General Assembly
summary_plain: Signed 21 March 2024 and effective 1 July 2024, the ELVIS Act updates Tennessee's Personal Rights Protection Act to add voice to the protected attributes of name, photograph and likeness, prohibits publishing or making available an individual's voice or likeness without authorisation, and creates liability for distributing or making available an algorithm, software or tool whose primary purpose is producing an individual's voice or likeness without authorisation. It provides civil actions for individuals and licensees and criminal penalties.

title: Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149, 89th Legislature)
issuing_body: Texas Legislature
summary_plain: Signed on 22 June 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, TRAIGA bans developing or deploying AI systems intended to manipulate people into self-harm or crime, government social scoring, biometric identification by government from public data without consent, intentional unlawful discrimination against protected classes, and production of child sexual abuse material or unlawful sexual deepfakes. State agencies and health-care providers must disclose AI interactions. It creates a 36-month regulatory sandbox administered by the Department of Information Resources, a Texas Artificial Intelligence Council, and gives the Attorney General exclusive enforcement with civil penalties after a 60-day cure period; disparate impact alone does not prove intent to discriminate.
who_it_applies_to: Developers and deployers of AI systems in Texas; state agencies; health-care providers using AI with patients.

title: Utah Artificial Intelligence Policy Act (SB 149, 2024, as amended by SB 226 and SB 332 in 2025)
issuing_body: Utah State Legislature
summary_plain: Effective 1 May 2024, the Act requires a person using generative AI to interact with a consumer in a consumer transaction to disclose clearly that the consumer is interacting with AI when asked (as amended in 2025, when the interaction is high-risk or on request), and requires providers of regulated occupations (for example health and legal services) to disclose generative-AI use proactively. It states that using AI is no defence to consumer-protection violations, created the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy and an AI learning laboratory allowing regulatory mitigation agreements, and originally sunset in 2025, extended to 2027.

title: Executive Order 14179: Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: President of the United States
summary_plain: Executive Order 14179, signed 23 January 2025, sets US federal policy to sustain and enhance American AI dominance, directs the development of an AI Action Plan within 180 days, and orders agencies to review and revise or rescind actions taken under the revoked Executive Order 14110 that are inconsistent with the new policy. It also called for revision of the OMB memoranda governing federal agency use and procurement of AI, which OMB replaced in April 2025 with M-25-21 and M-25-22.
who_it_applies_to: Federal executive departments and agencies; indirectly federal contractors and AI vendors.

title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) and Generative AI Profile
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (US Department of Commerce)
summary_plain: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is a voluntary framework for managing risks to individuals, organisations and society from AI. It organises practices into four functions: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, and describes characteristics of trustworthy AI such as validity, safety, security, accountability, explainability, privacy and fairness. The July 2024 Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) adds risks and suggested actions specific to generative AI. Many US procurement requirements and state laws reference the framework as a recognised approach.
who_it_applies_to: Any organisation that chooses to adopt it; referenced by regulators, state laws and customers.
source_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
issuing_body: Office of Management and Budget, Executive Office of the President
summary_plain: M-25-21 directs US federal agencies on how to govern and use AI. It requires agencies to designate Chief AI Officers, maintain AI governance boards, publish AI use-case inventories, and apply minimum risk-management practices to "high-impact" AI, including pre-deployment testing, AI impact assessments, ongoing monitoring, human oversight and training, and remedies for affected individuals. It replaced the 2024 memoranda with a greater emphasis on adoption and innovation while retaining core risk practices.
who_it_applies_to: Federal agencies, their Chief AI Officers, and by extension AI vendors and contractors.
source_reference: OMB memoranda index; reviewer to link the PDF directly

title: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
short_title: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
issuing_body: The White House (Office of Science and Technology Policy)
summary_plain: America's AI Action Plan is the federal AI strategy mandated by Executive Order 14179. It lists more than 90 policy actions grouped under three pillars: accelerating innovation (including removing regulatory barriers), building AI infrastructure such as data centres and chip fabrication with streamlined permitting, and leading internationally through AI exports and security measures. It was released with accompanying executive orders on federal procurement, data-centre permitting and AI exports.

title: Strategy for the development of artificial intelligence technologies until 2030 (Presidential Resolution, October 2024)
issuing_body: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
summary_plain: The 2024 resolution approves a strategy to 2030 to raise the AI services market, deploy AI in public administration and priority sectors, build data centres and datasets, train specialists and adopt ethical principles and standards for AI.

title: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 134/2025/QH15)
issuing_body: National Assembly of Vietnam
summary_plain: Vietnam's first dedicated AI statute, with eight chapters and 35 articles governing the research, development, provision, deployment and use of AI systems. It adopts a risk-based approach, requires human oversight in important decisions, and provides for national AI infrastructure, a national AI development fund, a regulatory sandbox and rules on AI-generated content. It took effect on 1 March 2026 with transition periods for existing systems.
source_publisher: Government of Vietnam legal document portal (vanban.chinhphu.vn)

title: National Strategy on Research, Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence to 2030 (Decision No. 127/QD-TTg)
short_title: National Strategy on Research, Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence to 2030
issuing_body: Prime Minister of Vietnam
summary_plain: A prime ministerial decision promulgating Vietnam's national AI strategy to 2030. It targets a top-four ASEAN and top-50 global position in AI, three national big data and high-performance computing centres, national innovation centres for AI and open datasets across sectors. It directs work on a legal framework, infrastructure, talent and application of AI in government and industry, with the Ministry of Science and Technology coordinating.
source_publisher: Government of Vietnam legal document portal (vanban.chinhphu.vn)

title: Zambia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Government of Zambia (Ministry of Technology and Science)
summary_plain: The strategy sets objectives on AI skills and research, adoption in public services, agriculture, health and mining, data infrastructure and responsible-AI governance.

title: Zimbabwe National Artificial Intelligence Policy
issuing_body: Government of Zimbabwe
summary_plain: The policy sets a framework for responsible AI adoption in government, agriculture, health, mining and education, skills and research, data governance and ethics.

title: Colorado Senate Bill 26-189: Automated Decision-Making Technology (replacement of the Colorado AI Act)
issuing_body: Colorado General Assembly
summary_plain: SB 26-189 replaces the Colorado AI Act's regulation of "high-risk" AI systems with duties that attach when automated decision-making technology materially influences a consequential decision about a Colorado consumer in areas such as employment, lending, housing, education, healthcare, insurance and government services. It drops the earlier duty of reasonable care, the mandatory risk-management programme, impact assessments and Attorney General notification, and substitutes advance notice to the consumer, disclosure after an adverse outcome, meaningful human review, three-year record keeping and developer documentation obligations.
who_it_applies_to: Developers and deployers of automated decision-making technology that materially influences consequential decisions about Colorado residents.

title: Abu Dhabi Government Digital Strategy 2025-2027
issuing_body: Abu Dhabi Executive Council
summary_plain: A AED 13 billion strategy to make Abu Dhabi a fully AI-native government by 2027, with targets including more than 200 AI solutions, full migration to a sovereign cloud and Chief Digital and AI Officers in every entity.
who_it_applies_to: Abu Dhabi government entities.

title: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10: personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems
issuing_body: Dubai International Financial Centre Authority
summary_plain: Sets rules for personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems in the Dubai International Financial Centre: notice and transparency when such a system is used, the deployer as controller and the operator as processor, limits on purposes, a future certification scheme, and an Autonomous Systems Officer for high-risk processing.
who_it_applies_to: Deployers and operators of AI systems processing personal data in the DIFC.

title: Dubai Universal Blueprint for Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Government of Dubai
summary_plain: An annual plan for AI in Dubai that includes appointing a Chief AI Officer in every government entity and a new commercial licence for AI companies.
who_it_applies_to: Dubai government entities; AI companies seeking a Dubai licence.

title: Buenos Aires Province Decree 742/2026: Provincial framework for the development, use and governance of artificial intelligence
short_title: Buenos Aires Province AI framework decree
issuing_body: Government of the Province of Buenos Aires
summary_plain: Sets the framework for AI in the provincial public sector, including risk and impact assessment and human oversight of decisions affecting rights. The Undersecretariat of Digital Government enforces it; it creates a provincial AI register and invites municipalities to adhere.
who_it_applies_to: Buenos Aires provincial public bodies; municipalities that adhere.
source_publisher: Normas de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

title: ACT Government Artificial Intelligence Policy (Version 1.0) and AI Assurance Framework
issuing_body: ACT Government
summary_plain: Aligns ACT government use of AI with Australia's AI Ethics Principles and the national assurance framework; in-scope initiatives are reviewed by an ACT AI Advisory Group, and standard AI features of commercial products are exempt.
who_it_applies_to: ACT Government directorates and agencies.

title: NSW AI Assessment Framework
issuing_body: Digital NSW
summary_plain: A risk-triage self-assessment across the AI lifecycle that replaced the NSW AI Assurance Framework. High- or critical-risk systems go to the AI Review Committee; using the assessment platform is mandatory for agencies under Circular DCS-2026-02.
who_it_applies_to: NSW government agencies.

title: NSW AI Operational Policy and Circular DCS-2026-02: Use of Artificial Intelligence by NSW Government Agencies
issuing_body: NSW Department of Customer Service
summary_plain: Replaces the NSW AI Ethics Policy and adopts Australia's AI Ethics Principles. Agencies must use the NSW AI Assessment Framework and give NSW GovAI a signed annual attestation by 31 October each year, the first due by 31 October 2027.
who_it_applies_to: NSW government agencies.

title: Work Health and Safety Amendment (Digital Work Systems) Act 2026 (NSW) (Act No 5 of 2026)
issuing_body: Parliament of New South Wales
summary_plain: Makes it a primary duty of a person conducting a business or undertaking to ensure that workers' health and safety is not put at risk by "digital work systems" (an algorithm, AI, automation or online platform), and lets WHS entry-permit holders ask to inspect those systems.
who_it_applies_to: NSW employers and other businesses or undertakings that use digital work systems.

title: Queensland Government Artificial Intelligence Governance Policy (QGEA)
issuing_body: Queensland Government Customer and Digital Group
summary_plain: Queensland departments must carry out a Foundational AI Risk Assessment (FAIRA, or FAIRA Lite for low-risk work, or an agreed equivalent) and set up AI governance with regard to ISO/IEC 38507.
who_it_applies_to: Queensland government departments.

title: South Australian Government Artificial Intelligence Ethics Policy (v1.0)
issuing_body: Government of South Australia
summary_plain: A mandatory policy requiring SA government agencies to align their AI systems with the Australian Government's AI Ethics Principles; a separate policy on responsible use and disclosure is being developed.
who_it_applies_to: South Australian government agencies.

title: Administrative Guideline for the safe and responsible use of Generative AI in the Victorian Public Sector (No. 2024/07)
short_title: Victoria public sector generative AI guideline
issuing_body: Department of Premier and Cabinet (Victoria)
summary_plain: Sets minimum requirements for generative AI in the Victorian public sector: agency-approved tools are preferred, AI should not be used to make decisions or assessments, privacy, FOI and human-rights obligations still apply, and staff must be trained. Relying on unverified AI output could breach the codes of conduct.
who_it_applies_to: Victorian public sector employees and bodies.

title: WA Government Artificial Intelligence Policy and Assurance Framework
short_title: Western Australia AI policy and assurance framework
issuing_body: Office of Digital Government (Western Australia)
summary_plain: Each WA public sector entity nominates an AI Accountable Officer and self-assesses its AI and automated decision-making systems; higher-risk, Digital Capability Fund-funded or large projects go to the WA AI Advisory Board, whose advice is non-binding, and use cases are recorded in a government AI register.
who_it_applies_to: Western Australian public sector entities.

title: Flemish Artificial Intelligence Policy Plan
issuing_body: Flemish Government
summary_plain: The Flemish government's AI programme, funding research, business adoption through VLAIO, and awareness, training and ethics. The first plan (2019) had about €32 million a year; a second cycle for 2024-2028 was approved in 2024.
who_it_applies_to: Organisations taking part in the Flemish AI programme.
source_publisher: Department of Economy, Science and Innovation (Flanders)

title: Goiás Complementary Law No. 205 of 19 May 2025: State Policy for the Promotion of Innovation in Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Legislative Assembly of Goiás
summary_plain: Promotes AI innovation, prefers open-source and open models in public AI projects, and gives people rights over automated decisions, including information, contestation and human review on appeal. It creates an AI ethics and innovation advisory body, a permanent state AI sandbox and an annual AI prize.
who_it_applies_to: Goiás state bodies, and organisations taking part in its AI programmes.
source_publisher: Casa Civil do Estado de Goiás

title: Paraná Law No. 22,324 of 2 April 2025: AI guidelines for the state public administration (PDIA/PR)
short_title: Paraná AI in public administration law
issuing_body: Legislative Assembly of Paraná
summary_plain: Requires AI used by the state executive to be ethical, transparent, explainable and auditable, with a regulatory sandbox and staff training; it also renamed the innovation department the Secretariat of Innovation and Artificial Intelligence. Decree 9854 of 7 May 2025 regulates the state AI council.
who_it_applies_to: Paraná state government bodies.

title: Government of Alberta Artificial Intelligence Usage Policy
issuing_body: Government of Alberta
summary_plain: Lets Alberta public servants use AI responsibly, within a list of approved AI platforms and use cases kept by the Ministry of Technology and Innovation; non-compliance can lead to discipline under the Public Service Act.
who_it_applies_to: Alberta public servants and ministries.

title: BC Public Service policy on the use of generative AI
short_title: British Columbia public service generative AI policy
issuing_body: Government of British Columbia
summary_plain: Bars BC public servants from entering confidential or personal information into public generative-AI tools, allows it only in tools covered by the government's Microsoft agreement when signed in with a government account, and requires staff to verify outputs.
who_it_applies_to: British Columbia public servants.

title: Beijing: Several Measures for Promoting the Innovation and Development of General Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: General Office of the Beijing Municipal People's Government
summary_plain: Twenty-one measures on compute, data, models, application scenarios and an "inclusive and prudent" approach to regulation and ethics for general-purpose AI in Beijing.
who_it_applies_to: Beijing municipal departments and AI companies.

title: Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on Promoting the Development of the Artificial Intelligence Sector
issuing_body: Standing Committee of the Shanghai Municipal People's Congress
summary_plain: Promotes the AI industry and names the economy and informatization department as lead regulator; sets up a strategy advisory committee and an AI ethics expert committee; bans certain uses such as discrimination and algorithmic price discrimination; applies list-based compliance review to high-risk AI products and disclosure with after-the-fact control to lower-risk ones; and allows sandbox supervision.
who_it_applies_to: AI developers, providers and users in Shanghai, and municipal authorities.

title: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Regulations on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry
issuing_body: Standing Committee of the Shenzhen Municipal People's Congress
summary_plain: Defines AI and the AI industry, sets up statistical monitoring and a municipal AI ethics committee, and allows trial access for low-risk AI products and services where no national or local standard exists yet.
who_it_applies_to: AI developers and providers in Shenzhen, and municipal authorities.

title: Schleswig-Holstein IT Deployment Act (ITEG): Act on the use of data-driven information technologies in public administration
issuing_body: Landtag of Schleswig-Holstein
summary_plain: Allows public administration to use AI and other data-driven IT as a general rule, with listed exclusions (for example, it may not be used to issue administrative acts involving discretion), and gives people a specific remedy, the "AI complaint" (KI-Rüge).
who_it_applies_to: Schleswig-Holstein public authorities using data-driven IT.

title: Catalonia AI Strategy 2030 (Estratègia Catalunya IA 2030)
issuing_body: Government of Catalonia
summary_plain: A five-year strategy with up to €1 billion and 90 actions across eight areas: infrastructure, talent, research, business adoption, the public sector, ethics, digital society and international projection. It replaces the Catalonia.AI strategy of February 2020.
who_it_applies_to: Catalan public bodies, research centres and businesses taking part in its programmes.

title: Extremadura Decree-law 2/2023 of 8 March on urgent measures to promote artificial intelligence
issuing_body: Junta de Extremadura
summary_plain: A framework to support and promote AI in Extremadura under principles of ethical and transparent AI; it required the regional government to adopt an Extremadura AI strategy within nine months.
who_it_applies_to: The Extremadura regional government and organisations taking part in its AI programmes.

title: Galician Law 2/2025 of 2 April for the development and promotion of artificial intelligence in Galicia
issuing_body: Parliament of Galicia
summary_plain: Sets the framework for how the Galician administration and regional public sector design, procure, deploy and use AI. It creates a Galician AI Office, a Galician AI Council and AI commissioners within departments, and provides for a regulatory sandbox and support for start-ups.
who_it_applies_to: The Galician regional administration and public sector bodies.

title: Hong Kong Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework (Digital Policy Office)
issuing_body: Digital Policy Office
summary_plain: Guiding principles, leading practices and an AI assessment for government AI projects, with a three-line governance model in which the IT board or chief information officer reviews high-risk AI. It was updated for generative AI.
who_it_applies_to: Hong Kong government bureaux and departments.
source_publisher: Digital Policy Office, Hong Kong SAR Government

title: Maharashtra Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026
issuing_body: Government of Maharashtra
summary_plain: An investment and adoption policy that targets about ₹10,000 crore of investment and 1.5 lakh jobs by 2031, with a Maharashtra AI Mission, an AI-adoption subsidy for MSMEs, an AI start-up venture fund, incubators, centres of excellence and AI innovation cities.
who_it_applies_to: Businesses, start-ups and institutions in Maharashtra taking part in its schemes.

title: Odisha Artificial Intelligence Policy 2025
issuing_body: Government of Odisha
summary_plain: A state AI policy built on four pillars (AI infrastructure, skills, energy and regulatory frameworks) with a dedicated Odisha AI Mission.
who_it_applies_to: Odisha government bodies and organisations in its AI programmes.

title: Tamil Nadu Safe and Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy 2020
short_title: Tamil Nadu Safe and Ethical AI Policy 2020
issuing_body: Information Technology Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
summary_plain: Recommends a six-dimension framework (TAM-DEF: transparency and audit, accountability and legal issues, misuse protection, digital divide and data deficit, ethics and fairness, equity) and a DEEP-MAX scorecard for deploying AI in government, with AI procurement guidelines.
who_it_applies_to: Tamil Nadu government departments and their AI suppliers.

title: Telangana's AI Framework (ITE&C Department)
issuing_body: Information Technology, Electronics and Communications Department, Government of Telangana
summary_plain: A six-pillar framework for AI in Telangana (data exchange; talent and education; research and innovation; high-performance computing; governance, ethics and privacy; adoption and community), run by the Telangana AI Mission with NASSCOM.
who_it_applies_to: Telangana government bodies and organisations in its AI programmes.

title: Calabria Regional Law No. 4 of 2 February 2026 on the use of artificial intelligence systems in the region
issuing_body: Regional Council of Calabria
summary_plain: Governs the use of AI in the regional administration, with human review, data protection and transparency; sets up a health-AI pilot programme, a voluntary regional register of AI developers and a regional AI Office.
who_it_applies_to: The Calabria regional administration and, on a voluntary basis, AI developers.

title: Tuscany regional law on the responsible and conscious use of artificial intelligence (approved 21 July 2026)
issuing_body: Regional Council of Tuscany
summary_plain: According to the regional government's news agency, the law creates a Tuscan charter of digital rights, a regional AI observatory supported by IRPET, and measures to protect minors.
who_it_applies_to: The Tuscany regional administration and bodies named in the law.

title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government AI Introduction and Utilization Guideline
issuing_body: Tokyo Metropolitan Government
summary_plain: Practical rules for Tokyo Metropolitan Government divisions adopting AI, including generative AI: a basic policy, six AI-specific cautions and a process from planning through procurement to retirement, with points graded as required or recommended. A staff handbook on generative AI was issued the same day.
who_it_applies_to: Tokyo Metropolitan Government divisions and staff.

title: Seoul Metropolitan Government Ordinance on Supporting AI Literacy Education
issuing_body: Seoul Metropolitan Council
summary_plain: A promotional ordinance under which the Seoul Metropolitan Government supports AI literacy education for citizens.
who_it_applies_to: The Seoul Metropolitan Government.

title: AI Tester Accreditation Programme (AI TAP)
issuing_body: AI Verify Foundation
summary_plain: Accredits third-party firms that test AI systems, in benchmarking and red teaming, for 12 months at a time; the first five were AIDX Tech, Knovel Engineering, PwC Singapore, Resaro and Vulcan. Accreditation does not certify that a tester is independent or that a tested system is safe.
who_it_applies_to: AI testing firms; organisations commissioning AI tests.

title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
issuing_body: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)
summary_plain: A governance framework for AI agents that reason and act on a user's behalf, in four areas: assessing and bounding risks upfront, making humans meaningfully accountable, technical controls across the agent lifecycle, and enabling end-user responsibility. IMDA treats it as a living document and has since added case studies and input from more than 50 organisations.
who_it_applies_to: Developers and deployers of agentic AI systems in Singapore and elsewhere.

title: Starter Kit for Testing Agentic Systems for Safety and Reliability
short_title: Singapore starter kit for testing agentic AI
issuing_body: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)
summary_plain: A practical reference for organisations starting to test AI agents that reason, act on a user's behalf, use tools and access data. It sets out four steps (identify risks such as erroneous or unauthorised actions; design and run realistic tests without real-world harm; analyse results and operational logs; monitor and retest continuously), tests the agent's whole trajectory of reasoning and actions rather than only its output, and suggests metrics such as tool-use accuracy, handoff accuracy and human-intervention rates. It extends the agentic AI governance framework and builds on the LLM starter kit.
who_it_applies_to: Developers, deployers and testers of AI agents.

title: Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0)
short_title: Singapore starter kit for testing LLM applications
issuing_body: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)
summary_plain: Voluntary guidelines for testing applications built on large language models against five risks: hallucination and inaccuracy, bias in decision-making, undesirable content, data leakage and adversarial prompts. Baseline tests are available on Project Moonshot.
who_it_applies_to: Developers, deployers and testers of LLM-based applications.

title: Northern Ireland's Draft Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: The Executive Office (Northern Ireland)
summary_plain: A draft strategy for responsible AI adoption across the Northern Ireland public sector under eight principles; the final version goes to the Executive.
who_it_applies_to: Northern Ireland departments and public bodies.

title: Scotland's AI Strategy 2026-2031
issuing_body: Scottish Government
summary_plain: A five-year strategy for responsible and inclusive AI growth, with ten early actions due by the end of March 2027, delivered through the AI Scotland programme. It builds on the 2021 strategy for trustworthy, ethical and inclusive AI.
who_it_applies_to: Scottish public bodies and organisations taking part in its programmes.

title: Scottish AI Register
issuing_body: Scottish Government
summary_plain: A public register of AI systems in use or in development in the Scottish public sector. The government announced in March 2024 that registration would become mandatory, starting with its own departments, but a 2025 freedom-of-information response describes the register as voluntary with an expectation that public bodies use it.
who_it_applies_to: Scottish public sector bodies.

title: AI Cymru: Shaping a Smarter, Fairer, More Prosperous Wales (AI plan for Wales)
issuing_body: Welsh Government
summary_plain: A plan built on four pillars (economic growth, educating Wales, equitable delivery, excellence and trust) with a Welsh Government Office for AI and a Strategic AI Advisory Group. It proposes no legislation.
who_it_applies_to: Welsh public bodies and organisations taking part in its programmes.

title: California AB 2013: Generative artificial intelligence: training data transparency (Chapter 817, Statutes of 2024)
issuing_body: California State Legislature
summary_plain: Developers of generative AI systems made available to Californians must post documentation of the data used to train them on their websites, including summaries of the datasets, whether they include copyrighted material, whether they were purchased or licensed, and whether they include personal information.
who_it_applies_to: Developers of generative AI systems and services offered to people in California.

title: California AI Transparency Act (SB 942, as amended by AB 853)
issuing_body: California State Legislature
summary_plain: Covered providers of generative AI systems must offer a free AI-detection tool and embed disclosures and provenance data in AI-generated content. AB 853 (Chapter 674, Statutes of 2025) moved the operative date to 2 August 2026 and added duties for large online platforms and generative-AI hosting platforms.
who_it_applies_to: Large generative-AI providers, and from 2027 large online platforms and generative-AI hosting platforms.

title: California Privacy Protection Agency regulations on automated decision-making technology, risk assessments and cybersecurity audits
issuing_body: California Privacy Protection Agency
summary_plain: Regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act on automated decision-making technology (ADMT), risk assessments and cybersecurity audits. Businesses that use ADMT to make significant decisions about consumers must comply from 1 January 2027, with further deadlines phased into 2028.
who_it_applies_to: Businesses subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act.

title: California SB 1119: Companion chatbots: children's safety (Chapter 190, Statutes of 2026)
issuing_body: California State Legislature
summary_plain: Operators must carry out a documented, child-focused risk assessment before releasing a new or substantially modified companion chatbot, from 1 July 2027, and commission child-safety audits by 1 January 2029 or before first public release if later. The Attorney General must set up a public incident-reporting mechanism by 1 January 2028.
who_it_applies_to: Operators of companion chatbots.

title: California SB 243: Companion chatbots (Chapter 677, Statutes of 2025)
issuing_body: California State Legislature
summary_plain: Operators of companion chatbots must disclose that the chatbot is AI and maintain a protocol for responding to suicidal ideation and self-harm that refers users to crisis services. Users known to be minors get break reminders and protection from sexual content. Annual reports to the Office of Suicide Prevention begin 1 July 2027, and a person injured by a violation can bring a civil action.
who_it_applies_to: Operators of companion chatbot platforms.

title: California SB 813: Independent verification organizations for AI (Chapter 179, Statutes of 2026)
issuing_body: California State Legislature
summary_plain: The Government Operations Agency must, by 1 January 2028, set up a process to designate and oversee independent verification organisations that assess AI models and applications. The law does not require any developer to use one.
who_it_applies_to: Prospective AI verification organisations and the Government Operations Agency.

title: Connecticut SB 5: An Act Concerning Online Safety (Public Act 26-15)
short_title: Connecticut online safety and frontier AI law (SB 5)
issuing_body: Connecticut General Assembly
summary_plain: A broad online-safety act that covers frontier developers, AI companions, AI in employment and synthetic content. Its frontier provisions bar retaliation against whistleblowers and require large frontier developers to set up an anonymous internal reporting process and report to their boards quarterly; no duty to publish a safety framework or transparency report was found.
who_it_applies_to: Frontier-model developers, AI companion operators and other businesses named in the act.

title: Illinois Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act (SB 315, Public Act 104-0538)
issuing_body: Illinois General Assembly
summary_plain: Illinois's frontier-AI safety and transparency law, built on the model of California SB 53: large frontier developers must publish a frontier AI framework and update it every year, publish a transparency report when they deploy a new or substantially modified frontier model, report critical safety incidents to the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security, and protect whistleblowing employees. Unlike the California and New York laws, it also requires annual independent third-party audits, with a published summary.
who_it_applies_to: Large frontier-model developers whose models are made available in Illinois.

title: Illinois Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act (HB 1806, Public Act 104-0054)
issuing_body: Illinois General Assembly
summary_plain: No one may provide therapy or psychotherapy in Illinois, including through AI, unless it is delivered by a licensed professional. AI may be used only for administrative and supplementary support, with notice to and consent from the client. The Department of Financial and Professional Regulation enforces it.
who_it_applies_to: Providers of therapy or psychotherapy services, including AI products marketed as therapy, and licensed professionals who use AI tools.

title: Kentucky SB 4 (2025): An Act relating to protection of information (Acts Chapter 66)
issuing_body: Kentucky General Assembly
summary_plain: The Commonwealth Office of Technology must create an AI Governance Committee, write AI policy and technology standards, and keep a registry of generative and high-risk AI used by state agencies. Agencies must disclose when AI is used in decisions about people or businesses and report every year. The act also creates a cause of action over synthetic media in election campaigns.
who_it_applies_to: Kentucky state agencies and the Commonwealth Office of Technology.

title: Maryland Artificial Intelligence Governance Act of 2024 (SB 818 / HB 1271, Chapter 496)
issuing_body: Maryland General Assembly
summary_plain: The Department of Information Technology sets AI policies for state government; state units must inventory their AI systems and carry out impact assessments, and public higher-education institutions must adopt AI policies.
who_it_applies_to: Maryland state government units and public universities and colleges.

title: Montana Right to Compute Act (SB 212, 69th Legislature, 2025)
issuing_body: Montana Legislature
summary_plain: Recognises a right to own and use computational resources and limits government restrictions on them; critical infrastructure facilities controlled by an AI system must have a risk management policy.
who_it_applies_to: Montana state and local government; operators of AI-controlled critical infrastructure.

title: New York AI companion safeguards (General Business Law Article 47, sections 1700-1701)
issuing_body: New York State Legislature
summary_plain: Operators of AI companions must have a protocol to detect and respond to suicidal ideation and self-harm, and must tell users they are talking to AI at the start of a session and at least every three hours.
who_it_applies_to: Operators of AI companion products.

title: Utah HB 452 (2025): Artificial Intelligence Amendments (mental health chatbots, Utah Code 13-72a)
issuing_body: Utah State Legislature
summary_plain: Mental health chatbots must disclose that they are AI; suppliers may not sell or share users' health information or input, or use it to target advertising. A written policy filed with the Division of Professional Licensing gives a supplier an affirmative defence.
who_it_applies_to: Suppliers of mental health chatbots.

title: Washington ESHB 2225: AI companion chatbots (Chapter 168, Laws of 2026)
issuing_body: Washington State Legislature
summary_plain: Operators must disclose that a companion chatbot is AI, repeat the notice hourly for known minors, limit sexual content and manipulative engagement tactics for minors, and keep and publish a self-harm protocol with crisis referrals. A violation is a violation of the Consumer Protection Act.
who_it_applies_to: Operators of AI companion chatbots.

title: Executive Order 14365: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: The White House
summary_plain: Directs the Attorney General to set up an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws, asks the Commerce Department to identify "onerous" state AI laws (with non-deployment broadband (BEAD) funds tied to that list), and asks the FTC for a policy statement on AI outputs. It does not itself pre-empt any state law; that would take legislation or a court ruling.
who_it_applies_to: Federal agencies; indirectly, states with AI laws and organisations relying on them.
